en: Agni has been awakened by the fuel of the people, facing the Dawn as she approaches like a milch-cow.
Like young birds springing up toward a branch, his rays stream forth toward the firmament.

The Hotṛ has been awakened for the sacrifice to the gods; Agni, well-disposed, has stood upright at dawn. The radiant splendor of the kindled one has been seen; the great god has been released from the darkness.
When he has awakened the tether of the host, the pure Agni anoints himself with pure rays of light;
then the strength-bestowing sacrificial fee is harnessed, and standing upright, he sucks at the outstretched ladles.
The minds of those seeking the gods turn toward Agni, just as eyes converge upon the sun;
when the two Dawns of different forms give birth to him, the white steed is born at the beginning of days.

For the Conqueror has been born at the beginning of days; the ruddy one has been placed among the woods that have been prepared. Bestowing seven treasures in every house, Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest.
Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest in the lap of his mother, in the fragrant place;
he is the youthful sage, established in many places, the observer of Truth, the sustainer of the peoples, kindled in their very midst.
Now they indeed magnify with obeisances that inspired priest, Agni, the excellent invoker at the sacrifices;
he who has stretched across heaven and earth by the Eternal Law—they ever groom the vigorous one with clarified butter.
The domestic friend, worthy of being groomed, is cleansed in his own home; he is our auspicious guest, praised by sages.
A bull with a thousand horns and such vigor, O Agni, you surpass all others by your might.
O Agni, you instantly surpass all others for whomever you have become most beautiful—
worthy of praise, wondrous, radiant, the beloved guest of human clans.
To you, O youngest Agni, the peoples bring tribute from near and from afar.
Take notice of the prayer of him who praises you most; great, vast, and auspicious is your protection, O Agni.
O Agni, mount first upon your radiant, shining chariot together with the worshipful ones;
knowing the paths, bring the gods here through the wide mid-air to eat the oblation.
We have spoken words of praise to the wise, holy bull, the showerer of blessings.
Gaviṣṭhira has offered with reverence a wide-reaching hymn to Agni, like a golden ornament set in the sky.
The youthful mother carries the boy hidden away in secret; she does not yield him to the father.
O people, they behold his face, which does not fade, placed before them upon the sacrificial ladle.
O young woman, whom do you carry as this boy? A secondary wife has borne him; the chief queen gave birth to him. For many autumns the embryo grew; I saw him born when his mother brought him forth.
I saw from afar him with golden teeth and pure luster, fashioning his weapons from the field;
giving him the mingled ambrosia, what can those who lack Indra and are devoid of hymns do to me?
From the field I saw him wandering from afar, like a well-fed herd, shining intensely.
They did not seize him, for he has been born; even the grey-haired women become young again.
Who are these who have separated my young bull from the cattle—those for whom there was no guardian, not even a stranger?
May those who have seized him release him; may he, the wise one, drive the herd toward us.
The enemies have hidden the King of the dwelling places, the abode of men, among mortals.
May the sacred prayers of Atri release him; let the revilers become themselves objects of reproach.
Even Śunaḥśepa, who had been bound as a victim, you released from the sacrificial post among a thousand; for he had performed his penance.
Even so, O Agni, release the bonds from us, O wise Hotṛ, having sat down here.
For you went away from me in anger; the guardian of the laws of the gods has told me:
"Indra, the knower, has indeed looked after you. Guided by him, O Agni, I have come here.
Agni shines with lofty light; by his greatness, he makes all things manifest.
He overcomes the godless, evil-wishing wiles; he sharpens his two horns to gore the Rakṣasa.
And let the roarings of Agni be in heaven, with sharp weapons to slay the Rakṣas;
even in his exhilaration, his splendors shatter [the foe]; the godless obstructors do not hold him back.
O many-born one, I, the inspired singer, have fashioned this hymn for you as a skillful craftsman fashions a chariot;
if you, O divine Agni, should accept it with favor, may we win through it the waters together with the light of heaven.
The bull with the thick neck, growing strong, shall gather the wealth of the enemy without a foe;
thus have the immortals spoken to this Agni: may he grant protection to the man who spreads the sacrificial grass; may he grant protection to the man who offers oblations.
O Agni, you are born as Varuṇa; when kindled, you become Mitra. In you, O Son of Strength, dwell all the gods; you are Indra for the mortal who offers oblations.
You become Aryaman when it concerns maidens; O self-dependent one, you bear a secret name. They anoint you like a well-placed Mitra with cows, when you bring the husband and wife into harmony.
For your glory, O Rudra, the Maruts have adorned themselves, for your birth is beautiful and wondrous.
That footprint of Viṣṇu which was set down as the highest—by that you guard the secret name of the cows.
O God, by your splendor the gods, being well-beheld, have attained immortality and serve you;
men have established Agni as the Hotṛ-priest, and the yearning ones, seeking to do honor, have seated him as the praise of living man.
O Agni, no Hotṛ priest before thee has been more skilled in sacrifice; none excels thee in wisdom, O self-dependent one.
And that mortal clan into which thou dost become a guest shall, through sacrifice, overcome other mortals, O God.
O Agni, protected by you, may we, seeking wealth and awakening with our oblation, overcome [our foes] in battle,
in the assemblies of days, and through riches, O Son of Strength, surpass mortals.
Whoever brings sin or offense against us, place that evil upon the one who seeks it;
O wise Agni, strike down this curse of him who harms us with duplicity.
O God, at the breaking of this dawn, the ancients, making you their messenger, worshipped you with oblations;
for when you, O Agni, go forth at the assembly of riches, you are a god kindled by mortals together with the Vasus.
Protect the father; fight as one who knows, O Son of Strength, for the son who has honored you.
When, O wise Agni, will you look upon us? When, as a knower of Truth (*ṛtacit*), will you bring us to fulfillment?
O Vasu, when the father offers many names in worship, if you take pleasure in that, will Agni— delighting in his divine power and having grown strong— not surely win favor?
O most youthful Agni, you indeed carry your singer across all difficulties;
thieves have been seen, and the treacherous people of unknown intent have become manifest.
These journeys have been directed toward you; indeed, this sin has been confessed before the Vasu.
This Agni shall not deliver us over to calumny, nor to the one who seeks to harm us, for he, having grown strong, will not give us up.
O Agni, King, I rejoice in you, the lord of treasures among all riches, at the sacrifices.
Through you, may we who strive for booty win the prize; may we overcome the hostile attacks of mortals.
Agni, the bearer of oblations, the ageless father of ours, is pervasive, radiant, and beautiful to behold among us.
With your excellent household-fire, shine forth upon us with nourishments; mete out for us glorious renown.
The sage of the tribes, the lord of human clans, the pure, purifying Agni whose back is anointed with ghee—you establish him as the all-knowing Hotṛ-priest; he wins desirable boons among the gods.
O Agni, being in harmony with the *iḷā* offering and striving in unison with the rays of the sun, be pleased;
O Jātavedas, accept our fuel and bring the gods here to eat the oblation.
Welcomed as the domestic friend and guest in the home, come to this our sacrifice, O wise one.
Having struck down all assailants, O Agni, bring hither the possessions of those who act as enemies.
Drive away the Dasyu with your weapon, creating strength for your own body;
since you, O Son of Strength, bring the gods across, protect us, O Agni, most heroic one, in the contest for booty.
O Agni, may we worship you with hymns; may we worship you with oblations, O Purifier of auspicious luster.
Bestow upon us wealth containing all boons; grant us all riches.
O Agni, Son of Strength, dweller in the three abodes, graciously accept our sacrifice and our oblation;
may we be doers of good among the gods, and protect us with your triple-layered shelter.
O Jātavedas, carry us across all difficulties as one crosses the ocean with a boat;
O Agni, being praised with homage like Atri, be the protector of our bodies.
O Jātavedas, you whom I, a mortal, calling upon you with a humble heart, invoke as the immortal one—bestow glory upon us; O Agni, may I attain immortality through my offspring.
O Agni Jātavedas, for that well-doer to whom you create a pleasant world,
he shall happily attain wealth consisting of horses, sons, heroes, and cattle.
Offer the sharp clarified butter to the well-kindled flame,
to Agni Jātavedas.
May Narāśaṃsa, the undeceivable one, prepare this sacrifice;
for he is the sage who holds the honey in his hand.
O Agni, being praised, bring hither the wonderful and beloved Indra on easy-gliding chariots for our protection.
Soft as wool, spread yourself out; the hymns have resounded toward you. O radiant one, be for our gain.
O divine doors, open yourselves wide for our easy passage and for our protection;
further and further extend the sacrifice.
We pray to the two mothers of Truth, the young ones with beautiful countenances who increase our vital strength— the Night and the Dawn.
Impelled by the flight of the wind, O two divine Hotṛ-priests of man,
come hither to this our sacrifice.
May Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī— the three goddesses who bring delight—
sit upon the sacrificial grass, they who are unfailing.
O Tvaṣṭṛ, come here as a benefactor; as a pervasive nourisher, protect us by your own self at every sacrifice.
O Lord of the Forest, wherever you know the secret names of the gods,
there bring our oblations.
Svāhā to Agni and Varuṇa; svāhā to Indra and the Maruts;
svāhā to the gods—the oblation!
I think of that Agni who is the Vasu, to whom the milch-cows go home, to whom the swift horses go home, and to whom the constant prize-winners go home; bring nourishment to those who praise you!
That Agni is the Vasu who is praised; he to whom the milch-cows come together, the swift-running steeds, and the well-born patrons; bring nourishment to those who laud you.
For Agni, the lord of all people, bestows a prize-winning steed upon the clan;
Agni grants wealth that is self-sustaining. Being well-pleased, he goes toward what is desirable; bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O Agni, we kindle you—the radiant, unaging god—so that this most wondrous fuel of yours may shine in heaven; bring nourishment to those who praise you.

To you, O Agni, Lord of the bright flame, an oblation is offered with a hymn—O radiant one, wonder-worker, Lord of the people, bearer of the sacrificial food—to you it is poured. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
Those Agnis among the fires nourish every desirable thing;
they are urged forward, they are incited, they hasten one after another. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O Agni, those flames of yours have grown great and powerful;
they who, with the leaps of their hooves, cause the stalls of cattle to tremble—bring nourishment to your praisers!
O Agni, bring new, well-established dwellings and nourishment to us who praise you.
May we be those who have sung your praises, having you as our messenger in every house; bring nourishment to those who laud you.
O you who are beautifully radiant, you mix both ladles of clarified butter in your mouth;
therefore, O Lord of Might, fill us up during our hymns and bring nourishment to those who praise you.
Thus have they constantly honored this ageless Agni with songs and sacrifices.
May he bestow upon us great heroic strength and that very abundance of swift horses; bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O friends, bring together for Agni— him who is the highest among the dwellings of the people, the offspring of strength, and the powerful one— your nourishment and your hymn of praise in unison.
In whose gathering men rejoice wherever they are seated among heroes;
whom even those worthy of honor kindle, and whom all living beings bring forth together.
When we gather together the sacrificial foods and the oblations of men,
he seizes for himself the ray of light, the power of glory, and the truth.
He indeed raises his banner even by night for him who stays afar;
when the ageless purifier consumes the lords of the forest.
In whose service they pour forth sweat upon the paths,
him indeed have the people mounted as if upon the back of a noble steed.
Him whom the mortal man, much-desiring, has established for the sustenance of all—
the one who provides the relish of nourishments and a dwelling even for the living man.
For he indeed cuts down the desert that has grown barren, like a beast that sheds its skin;
golden-bearded, pure-toothed, skillful, and of unimpaired vigor.
Pure indeed, he flows forth like the axe from him, as did Atri;
well-born, the mother has brought him forth when, active, he attained his portion.
O Agni, you who are invoked with clarified butter, that which is yours for our nourishment brings us peace;
bestow upon these mortals splendor, renown, and inspired thought.
Thus indeed did the noble one take away the fury [of the enemy] and seize the cattle given by you;
then, O Agni, may Atri overcome the Dasyus who do not give, and may he overcome the men who withhold food.
O Agni, those seeking the cosmic order have kindled you—the ancient one, for the sake of aid, O you who are strengthened by power.
You are the many-shining, worshipful, all-sustaining, domestic, lord of the house, and most excellent.

O Agni, the people have established you as their ancient guest, the flame-haired lord of the household; you who possess lofty banners, manifold forms, and win wealth—you who grant excellent protection, provide good shelter, and consume the aged.
O Agni, the human tribes invoke you, the knower of the sacrificial office, the discerning one, the greatest bestower of jewels;
you who, though dwelling in secret, O blessed one, are visible to all, loud-sounding, worthy of excellent sacrifice, and resplendent with ghee.
O Agni, we have approached you, the sustainer, with songs from every side and with reverence;
as such, O Aṅgiras, being kindled, take pleasure in us—a god for the mortal—with glorious and beautiful splendors.
O Agni, you who possess many forms, bestowing vital strength upon every clan as of old, O much-praised one;
you rule over many foods by your might. That brilliance of yours, as you blaze forth, is not to be assailed.
O Agni, youngest of the gods, when you were kindled, the gods made you their messenger, the bearer of oblations;
they established you—wide-striding, with ghee as your womb, invoked, brilliant, and impelling the thought—as their eye.
O Agni, from of old, those seeking favor have kindled you with ghee and excellent fuel when you were invoked;
thus, having grown strong and nourished by the plants, you spread yourself abroad over the terrestrial expanses.
O Agni, mortals bearing oblations invoke you, the god;
I acknowledge you as Jātavedas, for you shall carry the offerings in due order.
Agni is the Hotṛ-priest of the generous patron who has trimmed the sacrificial grass;
he is the one toward whom all sacrifices proceed, and all strengths that seek renown.
And him whom the kindling-sticks have brought forth like a newborn infant—
the Agni who sustains the human tribes and performs the sacrifice well.
And you are indeed difficult to seize, like the son of those who wander;
O Agni, you who burn many forests like an animal in a pasture.
Now, his smoky flames come together completely,
when Trita, as if at the divine [heaven], blows upon him like a smith, sharpening him as a smith would.
O Agni, through your protections and through the praises of Mitra,
may we overcome the ill-fortune and the enmities of mortal men.

O Agni, bring that wealth to us, O heroic one, through your power; may it provide for our dwelling and our prosperity, and may it lead to the winning of strength. And do you stand by us for our increase in battles.
O Agni, bring us the most powerful splendor, O irresistible one! Open for us a path to wealth and abundance, and to strength.
O wondrous Agni, through your wisdom and the greatness of your power, the divine might has ascended in you; acting as a friend, you are worthy of sacrifice.
O Agni, increase for us the household and the prosperity of these men,
the patrons who, through their hymns of praise, have attained great riches.
O Agni, those men who, possessing the gift of horses, adorn their songs for you, O radiant one;
they are powerful through their own vigor—men whose great fame awakens by itself even from heaven.
O Agni, those flames of yours go forth boldly, shining brightly like lightning-flashes that traverse the sky, or like a rattling chariot seeking the prize.
Now, O Agni, come for our protection and for the granting of gifts to us who press on;
and may our wise patrons cross over all regions.

O Agni Aṅgiras, you who have been praised and are being lauded, bring to us, O Hotṛ, wealth that overcomes the mighty; for our sake, you are being praised by those who laud you, and may you stand as our strengthener in battles.
The guardian of the people, the watchful Agni, the highly skillful, has been born for new-found prosperity.
With his face anointed with ghee, reaching to the great heavens, he shines brilliantly and purely for the Bharatas.
Men have kindled Agni, the banner of sacrifice, the first domestic priest, in his threefold seat;
seated upon the sacrificial grass together with Indra and the gods on the same chariot, he, the wise Hotṛ, sits down for the performance of the sacrifice.
Unrubbed, you are born pure from your two mothers; as a delightful sage, you have arisen from Vivasvat.
With clarified butter they strengthened you, O Agni, when you were invoked; your smoke became a banner resting in heaven.
May Agni come straight to our sacrifice; men carry Agni hither and thither from house to house.
Agni has become the messenger, the bearer of oblations; choosing Agni, they choose him who possesses the wisdom of a seer.
For you, O Agni, let this speech be most sweet; for you let this inspired thought be a blessing to the heart.
As great rivers fill the ocean, so do our songs fill you and increase you with power.
O Agni, the Aṅgirases found you hidden in secret, dwelling in every forest;
being churned, you are born with great power, and they call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength.
To Agni, the great and worshipful, the bull of *ṛta*, the Asura, I bring this prayer;
like well-purified ghee in the mouth at the sacrifice, I offer this song directed toward the Bull.
O knower of *ṛta*, take heed of *ṛta*; pierce open the many streams of *ṛta*. I do not pursue the sorcerer by force nor through deceit; I follow the *ṛta* of the ruddy bull.
By what [means], O Agni, acting according to *ṛta* through *ṛta*, do you become the knower of our new hymn?
O God, protector of the seasons, you know my seasons; I do not know the master of this wealth that he wins.
Who, O Agni, are your bondsmen for the enemy? Who, as radiant protectors, shall win the prize?
Who, O Agni, drink the nourishment of falsehood? Who are the guardians of the speech of the liar?
O Agni, these companions of yours have turned away; though they were once auspicious, they have become inauspicious.
They have harmed themselves by their own words, uttering crooked things against you who act with rectitude.
O Agni, he who honors your sacrifice with reverence protects the *ṛta* of the ruddy bull;
may his dwelling be broad and successful, the lineage of Nahuṣa as he spreads forth.
Praising you, we call upon you; praising you, we kindle you. O Agni, praising you, [we call] for your aid.
O Agni, we fashion today an effective hymn for you, the one who touches the heavens, as we, desiring wealth, seek the riches of the god.
May Agni, who is the Hotṛ among men, take pleasure in our songs; may he worship the divine host.
O Agni, you are far-extending, the beloved and excellent Hotṛ;
through you, they spread out the sacrifice.
O Agni, the inspired singers magnify you, the best winner of booty, who are well-praised;
as such, grant us great heroic strength.
O Agni, as the felly encompasses the spokes, you encompass the gods;
you strive for wondrous wealth.
Awaken Agni with a hymn of praise, kindling the immortal one;
may he place our offerings among the gods.
At the sacrifices, mortals invoke that immortal god,
the best of sacrificers among the human race.
For him indeed all people constantly invoke with the ladle dripping with clarified butter—
the god Agni, so that he may carry their oblations.
Agni, once born, shone forth, slaying the Dasyus and dispelling darkness with his light; he found the cattle, the waters, and the sun.
Worship Agni, the seer worthy of invocation, whose back is anointed with ghee;
may he come and hear my call.
They have magnified Agni, who belongs to all people, with clarified butter, with hymns, and with well-composed,
eloquent words.
I offer a song of praise to the ordainer, the seer, the one worthy of being known, to the glorious and ancient one.
Agni is the Asura who sits upon the clarified butter, the very gracious one, the sustainer of wealth, the upholder of all treasure.

By means of *ṛta* they have established the supporting foundation of *ṛta*, through the power of the sacrifice in the highest heaven. Seated upon the support of the laws of heaven, those who have reached the unborn by means of the born have surpassed all men.
The seekers of aid extend their bodies for him; great and invincible is his vital power for the Ancient One.
May he, newly born, overcome the enclosures; they stand around him on all sides like a lion in a rage.
As a mother, when you spread yourself out, you bear every person for their nourishment and for their vision;
assuming life after life for their aging, you move about by your own power in manifold forms.
May Vāja protect the limit of your power; O God, you have milked out a wide and enduring support for wealth.
Like a thief concealing his footprint in a cave, you have reached Atri, making him mindful of great riches.
Sing forth a great hymn of praise to the radiant god Agni,
whom mortals have placed in the forefront like a friend with their eulogies.
For he, Agni, by the days of men, is the Hotṛ-priest within the arms of Dakṣa; he, like Bhaga, distributes the sacrificial offering in due order as a desirable boon.
In the praise-song of this liberal lord, in the friendship of him whose radiance has increased— him,
the loudly roaring noble one, in whom all [the gods] have placed their strength.
For now, O Agni, by the greatness of their heroic power,
both heaven and earth have encompassed his fame, as if he were a mighty youth.
Now come to us, O Agni, being praised; bring us what is desirable.
May we and our wise patrons together establish ourselves in well-being; and do thou stand by us for our increase in battles.
O God, with sacrifices, let the mortal thus entreat the most powerful Agni for protection, when the rite is well-prepared, so that Pūru may be aided.
For by his own most glorious mouth, O Vidharman, you are esteemed;
him, the vault of heaven with wondrous luster, the delightful one, [I praise] beyond [all] with my inspired thought.
His garments indeed [shine] with flame, he who has been yoked by the impetuous song;
whose lofty rays blaze like the seed of heaven.
Through the wisdom of this wondrous one, the wise, wealth has come upon his chariot;
thus Agni, who is to be invoked among all the people, is praised.
Now indeed, O Son of Strength, let the wise patrons attend to our desirable wealth with their mouths;
protect us for our aid, grant us power for our well-being, and stand up for our increase in battles.
At dawn, may Agni, the beloved of many, be praised as the guest of the people—
he, the immortal one, who delights in all the oblations among mortals.
For Dvita, who carries away what is injured through the greatness of his own skill— O Immortal One, even your praiser provides the Soma-drop to him in due succession.
With my song, I invoke for you that one whose flame is long-lasting, among the wealthy patrons, whose chariot— unharmed and bestowing horses— advances far and wide.
Those in whom there is brilliant insight, who protect the hymns of praise,
they have spread the sacrificial grass for Svarṇara and have established glorious renown around them.

O Agni, you who dwell in common praise with those who have given me fifty horses— bestow upon these wealthy patrons, O immortal one, brilliant, great, and lofty glory that is like that of heroes among men.
The various states come forth; from the enclosure, the enclosure has become manifest. He gazes out from the lap of his mother.
Observing clearly, they have offered oblations; with unblinking eyes, they guard their manly vigor.
They have entered the firm fortress.
The people of Śvaitreya, the tribes, have increased in splendor; Niṣkagrīva, Bṛhaduktha, seeks booty with this sweet draught as it were.
Like beloved, desirable milk, [he is] the non-kin together with the two kinsmen;
like a cauldron filled with strength, he is undeceived and the deceiver of all.
Playing, O Flame, come to us, finding union with the ash and the wind;
those flames of his, sharp like spears and well-whetted, stand upon the breast of the wood.
O Agni, best winner of booty, whatever wealth you yourself deem worthy,
make that renowned among the gods for us through our songs, as a companion to be praised.
O Agni, those who do not bring down [the gods] for you, though they have grown great through fierce power— they pursue the hatred and the crookedness of one who follows another's law.
We choose you as the Hotṛ, O Agni, the accomplisher of skill;
at the sacrifices, bringing offerings, we invoke you with song as the one who is foremost.
Thus, O powerful one, so that we may be for your aid day by day—for wealth and for the cosmic order, O wise one—may we be sharers of the feast with cattle; may we be sharers of the feast with heroes.
Like Manu, we set thee down; like Manu, we kindle thee.
O Agni, O Aṅgiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
For you, O Agni, are kindled with great delight among the human race;
the ladles approach you in succession, O well-born one, whose libations are poured with clarified butter.
All the gods, acting in unison, have made you their messenger;
honoring you, O Sage, they invoke you as a god at the sacrifices.
Let the mortal worship Agni, your god, with the sacrifice to the gods.
Kindled, O radiant one, shine forth; you have sat upon the seat of Ṛta, you have sat upon the seat of the sacrificial grass.
O Viśvasāman, like Atri, sing forth to him of purifying luster,
who is to be praised at the sacrifices as the most delightful Hotṛ-priest among the people.
Set down Agni Jātavedas, the god and the officiating priest;
let the sacrifice proceed today in due order, most spacious for the gods.
O God of conscious mind, we mortals have meditated upon you for our protection; seeking your most excellent aid, we have called upon you.
O Agni, O powerful one, take note of this our speech!
O fair-cheeked lord of the household, the Atris increase you with hymns; the Atris adorn you with songs of praise.
O Agni, by the force of your splendor, bring hither conquering wealth—
wealth that shall overcome all peoples in the contests for booty through your presence.
O Agni, bring hither that wealth which overcomes hostile armies,
for you are the true and wondrous giver of booty consisting of cattle.
For all people, with one accord, having spread the sacrificial grass, seek you—
the beloved invoker in their dwellings— for many desirable boons.
For he indeed, the one who belongs to all people, has taken up overwhelming power against the assailant.
O Agni, shine richly for us in these dwellings; O bright one, shine with splendor; O purifier, shine forth!
O Agni, be our closest friend, our protector, and our auspicious guardian.
Agni is the Vasu, possessed of Vasu-glory; come hither and grant us most resplendent wealth.
Be mindful of us; hear our call; deliver us from every one who intends us harm.
O most radiant one, O shining one, we now entreat you for the welfare of our friends.
I sing toward Agni, the god, for your protection; may he, our benefactor, grant us wealth.
May the son of the *ṛṣis*, the upholder of *ṛta*, bestow gifts and carry us across our enemies.
For he is the true one, whom the men of old and even the gods kindled—
the Hotṛ-priest with the lovely tongue, rich in splendor through his brilliant lights.
O Agni, worthy of choice, shine wealth upon us through our most excellent prayer and through your most sublime favor, O you who are praised with well-fashioned hymns.
Agni reigns among the gods; Agni enters into mortals. Agni is our bearer of oblations; honor Agni with your prayers.
Agni bestows upon the worshipper a son who possesses most abundant fame, who is a supreme priest of powerful prayer, and who is an unconquered lord of renown.
Agni bestows a lord of the settlement, he who conquers with his men in battle;
Agni [bestows] a swift-gliding steed, a victor unconquered.
Sing forth a great hymn to Agni, O Vibhāvasu, that which is most effective;
from you wealth issues like a mighty cow, and from you the spoils of war arise.
Your radiant rays resound mightily like the pressing-stones; and your roar has gone forth of its own accord from heaven like thunder.
Thus, seeking wealth, we have praised Agni, the victorious one;
may he, the wise one, carry us across all enemies as if with a ship.
O Agni, purifier, with your radiance and your pleasant tongue, O god,
bring the gods here and worship them.
We pray to you, O Agni, whose back is dripping with ghee, O you of wondrous luster, who behold the light of heaven;
bring the gods here for the feast.
O Sage, we kindle you, the one who accepts the oblation, the radiant one,
O Agni, the great one at the sacrifice.
O Agni, come with all the gods for the giving of the oblation;
we choose you as our Hotṛ-priest.
O Agni, bring heroic vigor to the sacrificer who presses the soma;
sit down upon the sacrificial grass together with the gods.
Kindled, O Agni, winner of thousands, you nourish the sacred laws;
you are the praiseworthy messenger of the gods.
Establish Agni Jātavedas, the bearer of the oblation, the youngest,
the divine officiant.
Let the sacrifice proceed in due order today, most spacious for the gods;
strew the sacrificial grass for them to sit upon.
May the Maruts, the Aśvins, Mitra, and Varuṇa sit here; may the gods sit with their entire host.
The lord of the virtuous has bestowed upon me two oxen with a wagon; the most wise Asura among the wealthy ones is he.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, Tryaruṇa, the son of Trivṛṣan, has distinguished himself with ten thousand gifts.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, well-praised and increasing in strength, grant protection to Tryaruṇa— he who gives me one hundred and twenty cows and two bay horses, well-yoked and easy to drive.
Thus Trasadasyu, desiring your favor, O Agni, has offered this newest song for the ninth time to you,
the most youthful one— Trayaruna, who with a yoked [chariot] extols my many ancient hymns, I who am of mighty birth.
Whoever shall speak thus for me, for the wise Aśvamedha:
"He gives a gift to the one who seeks gain with a hymn; he gives wisdom to the one who follows the cosmic order."
He whose hundred dappled bulls exhilarate me,
like the gifts of Aśvamedha, like Soma juices mixed with threefold milk.
O Indra and Agni, bestow upon Aśvamedha, the giver of a hundredfold, great heroic power and a vast dominion, like the unaging sun in the sky.
Enkindled, Agni has sent his flame to heaven; facing the Dawn, he shines far and wide.
Rich in all boons, anointed with ghee, she goes eastward toward the gods with salutations, praising them with the oblation.
Being kindled, you reign as the sovereign of immortality; you attend to the one who prepares the oblation for his well-being.
He whom you impel gains all wealth; O Agni, you establish him as a guest of honor before [the gods].
O Agni, be bold for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent.
Bring together a household that is easy to govern, and trample down the powers of those who act as enemies.
O Agni, I praise the splendor of you who have been kindled with great majesty;
you are a bull, full of luster, and are enkindled at the sacrifices.
O Agni, kindled and invoked with oblations, perform the sacrifice to the gods in this well-conducted rite;
for you are the bearer of the offerings.
Offer oblations and serve Agni as the sacrifice proceeds; choose him as the bearer of the offerings.
Aryaman sustains the three divine realms at the assembly of the gods for man;
the Maruts, whose will is purified, sing praises to you—you, O Indra, are their wise seer.
When the Maruts sang in praise of Indra as he rejoiced after drinking of the pressed soma, he seized his thunderbolt to strike the dragon; he released the mighty waters so that they might flow.
And may the Maruts, the holy ones, and Indra drink of this well-pressed Soma for me;
for that is the oblation which found the cattle for Manu, and having drunk it, Indra slew the serpent.
He propped apart the two worlds more widely; even as he enveloped them, he struck terror into the wild beast.
Indra, casting out the devourer, struck down the Dānava who was panting against him.
Then, O Maghavan, by your will all the gods yielded to you the drinking of Soma,
when you brought the flying bay mares of the Sun, which were in front, down behind Etaśa.
When Maghavan, with his thunderbolt, simultaneously shattered his ninety-nine coils, the Maruts praised Indra at the assembly; with a Triṣṭubh hymn, they forced open the sky.
As a friend for his friend, Agni quickly cooked three hundred buffaloes by means of his will.
Indra, for the sake of slaying Vṛtra, drank the pressed Soma together with three lakes from Manu.
When Maghavan drank three hundred buffaloes' worth of Soma and three lakes of it,
all the gods raised a shout for Indra, as for a prize, when he slew the dragon.
When Uśanas and you, O Indra, came to the house with powerful, swift-running horses, you went there on the same chariot with Kutsa, conquering; indeed, with the gods, you overthrew Śuṣṇa.
You pulled away one wheel of the sun and provided the other space for Kutsa to travel;
you crushed the noseless Dasyus with your weapon and cast down those of insulting speech into their own dwelling-place.
The hymns of Gaurivīti magnified you; you delivered Pipru over to Vaidathina.
Ṛjiśvan turned to you for friendship; cooking sacrificial cakes, he drank his soma.
The Navagvas and Daśagvas, having pressed the Soma, honor Indra with their hymns;
even that stall of cattle which was securely closed, the men, exerting themselves, have opened.
How indeed, O Maghavan, shall I, though knowing, extol all those heroic deeds which you have performed?
And those new ones which you, O Most Mighty One, shall now accomplish—let us proclaim them forth to you in the assemblies.
O Indra, you who have performed all these many deeds from birth, unopposed by any in heroism—
whatever bold acts you now perform, O wielder of the thunderbolt, there is no one who can withstand that power of yours.
O Indra, most powerful one, take pleasure in the prayers being performed for you, these new ones which we have fashioned for you.
Like well-made, auspicious garments, I—seeking wealth like a skillful craftsman—have fashioned them as a wise man fashions a chariot.

Where is that hero? Who has seen Indra, approaching with his easy-rolling chariot and his two bay horses—he, the wielder of the thunderbolt, who, seeking the one who has pressed the soma with wealth, comes as a much-invoked protector to that dwelling for the sake of aid?
I have declared his secret, powerful place; seeking it, I followed the track of the one who deposited it.
I questioned others, and they said to me: "May we, as men awakened, attain Indra."

Now, O Indra, let us proclaim at the libation those deeds of yours which you have performed and which you have graciously accepted from us. May he who knows not take heed, and may he who knows listen; here comes the Bounteous Lord with his entire host.
O Indra, as soon as you were born, you made your mind firm; seeking battle alone against even many, you by your might shattered the rock and found the cave of the ruddy cows.

When you, the supreme one, were born in the far distance, bearing a name renowned afar, even from that Indra the gods were struck with fear; he conquered all the waters that had the Dāsas as their masters.
For you, O Indra, these most gracious Maruts sing their hymn of praise and press the Soma juice;
may Indra, by his wondrous powers, overcome the guileful one who dwells within the waters, the serpent who lies coiled and hidden.
From birth, you have driven away the scorners, O Maghavan, bestowing gifts and delighting in cattle;
there, seeking a path for Manu, you struck off the head of the Dāsa Namuci.
For you have indeed made me your ally, O Indra, while you were crushing the head of the Dāsa Namuci;
like a whirling stone, you cast both heaven and earth apart for the Maruts.
For Dāsa made women his weapons; what could his weak armies do to me?
He perceived both his milch-cows within, and then Indra went forth to fight the Dasyu.
Here the cows lowed together from all sides, having been separated here and there from their calves;
Indra reunited them by his powers when the well-pressed Soma juices exhilarated him.
When the brown Soma juices, shaken [in the filter], exhilarated him, the bull bellowed loudly at his seats. Having drunk of this, Indra, the breaker of forts, gave back the ruddy cows.
This was a good deed, O Agni, which the Ruśamas have done, giving away four thousand cattle.
We have accepted the offered riches of Ṛṇañcaya, the most heroic among men.
The Ruśamas, O Agni, have released me well-adorned into my home with thousands of cattle.
At the dawning of the night’s end, the strong pressed juices have exhilarated Indra.
That night, which was destined to end, dawned for R̥ṇañcaya, the king of the Ruśamas;
like a swift, prize-winning steed urged forward, Babhru won four thousand.
We have received four thousand head of cattle from among the Ruśamas, O Agni;
even the heated cauldron which was there for the Pravargya rite, that iron one, we wise ones have taken up.
Indra, the Bounteous One, prepares an easy slope for the chariot upon which he has mounted as it strives for booty.
Like a herdsman driving his cattle, he opens the way; uninjured and seeking to win, he goes as the first.
Come running hither, O Lord of the Bay Steeds; do not be reluctant, but attend to us, O giver of golden wealth!
For there is nothing better than you, O Indra; even those who were born of the unyielding [stone], you have brought under your power.
When his strength was born from strength, Indra displayed all his Indra-powers.
He drove forth the well-milking cows within the enclosure; with light, he rolled away the encompassing darkness.
The Anus have fashioned a chariot for your horse; Tvaṣṭṛ, O much-invoked one, has forged the radiant thunderbolt.
The priests, magnifying Indra with their hymns, strengthened him for the slaying of the serpent.
When the strong ones sang their hymn of praise to you, the Strong One, O Indra—the pressing-stones and Aditi acting in harmony;
then the fellies, though without horses and without chariots, driven by Indra, rolled against the Dasyus.
I shall proclaim your former deeds and those new ones, O Maghavan, which you have performed:
that you, O mighty one, supported both heaven and earth, and winning the waters of wondrous bounty for Manu.
That indeed was your deed, O wonder-worker, O sage—when slaying the dragon, you measured out your power;
you seized even the wiles of Śuṣṇa, and advancing, you drove away the Dasyus.
O Indra, you stayed the well-milking waters for Yadu and Turvaśa on the far shore.
You went forth with fierce power; you brought Kutsa, when the gods and Uśanas came together to meet you both.
O Indra and Aṅgiras, as you travel on your chariot, let your coursers carry you even to our ear.
You blow [the darkness] away from the waters and from their dwelling places; you drive the gloom from the hearts of the generous patrons.
Even a seer has come here seeking help, desiring the well-yoked horses of the wind.
O Indra, all the Maruts were your friends there; they increased your power through their sacred hymns.
Even the Sun, in the final race, shall place his chariot behind the one who has sped forward; Etaśa shall bring the wheel and join it on, placing it in front—he will win for us our purpose.
O people, Indra has come hither to behold you, seeking his friend who has pressed the soma;
the pressing-stone speaks as it is brought to the altar, and for him the Adhvaryu priests move with haste.

Those mortals who have desired you and continue to desire you, O Immortal One—may they not fall into distress. Honor those who offer sacrifice, and bestow vigor upon those people among whom we may be numbered.
You burst open the spring; you released the channels; you set at rest the obstructed floods.
O Indra, when you shattered the great mountain, you released the streams downward and struck down the Dānava.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, you set in motion the springs of the mountain’s udder, which were obstructed by the seasons;
having struck down even the fierce, writhing serpent as he lay there, O Indra, you displayed your might.
Even from that great beast, Indra struck down the deadly weapon with his powers;
he who alone was considered matchless, yet another, even stronger than he, was born after him.

The wielder of the thunderbolt, with his impetuous onset, struck down Śuṣṇa— the son of Mīḍhuḥ, who revels by his own will among these [waters], who prospers in the mist and moves in darkness— with his bolt against the fury of the Dānava.
By his very powers of will, he has struck the vital organ of that one who was seated there unvulnerable;
for when you, O Lord of Good Dominion, had presented the exhilarating draught, you placed him who sought to fight within the darkness of the dwelling.
Even him who was thus lying prostrate, growing strong in sunless darkness,
even him Indra, exhilarated by the pressed juice, having raised his arm aloft, struck down.
When Indra raised his irresistible weapon against the great Dānava,
at the hurling of the thunderbolt he struck him down and reduced every living creature to the lowest state.
The fierce one seized that very honey-drinking wave which lay coiled and motionless;
with his great weapon, he cast down the footless devourer, the speaker of falsehood, into a narrow pit.
Who can withstand his fury and his might? He alone, unopposed, carries off the spoils of wealth. Even these two goddesses, the expanses of heaven, flee in fear before the power of Indra’s strength.

The divine axe bows down before him; for Indra, the path has opened like one longing [for him]. When he gathers all power together with these [fingers], the peoples bow down before him, the self-dependent one.
I hear that you alone are the lord of the virtuous, born as the protector of the five peoples, renowned among men.
Him, Indra, the newest one, our prayers have grasped; calling upon him at evening and at dawn, we seek his favor.
For thus indeed I hear of you as bestowing gifts upon the inspired singers at the proper season, giving wealth to the wise.
What do those Brahmins gain for you, O Indra, who as friends have fulfilled your desire?

I meditate upon the great one for the sake of the great and powerful Indra, the manly one; thus does the weakling [strive] for the powerful one—[Indra], who, being praised among the people, takes notice of this man’s good intent in the winning of booty during the battle.
So, O Indra, being mindful of us through our hymns, O Bull, you have harnessed the pair of bay steeds;
for you, O Maghavan, according to your pleasure, shall drive toward those who come to you, and you shall overcome the people.
O Indra, those lofty ones of yours shall not remain unyoked by us through lack of prayer;
mount that chariot, O wielder of the thunderbolt, for you, O God with noble steeds, hold the reins.
O Indra, since many hymns have been offered to you, you who fought for cattle in the fertile lands;
like a bull in his own dwelling, you fashioned even the name of the Dāsa in the battles for the sake of Sūrya.
We are yours, O Indra, as are these men—your host who have been born and your chariots that have gone forth.
May he whose strength is like a serpent come to us, a hero to be invoked like Bhaga, dear in our offerings at the distribution of wealth.
O Indra, you have filled yourself with strength that must be satisfied, for you, the immortal, displaying manly vigor;
as such, O possessor of wealth, grant us brilliant riches—I praise the gift of the one of abundant bounty.
Thus, O Hero Indra, protect us with your aids; favor the singers and poets who praise you.
And at the winning of booty, be pleased with those who offer the skin of the well-pressed, sweet, and delightful soma.
And may those ten white horses of Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, the lord who is rich in gold, carry me away as they grant their gifts; may I now be united with the wills of Gairikṣita.
And those red steeds of Mārutāśva, who through their will are givers of wealth at the distribution of the assembly—
Cyavatāna, giving me thousands, has sung in praise for the beauty of the noble one’s lineage.
And those well-pleasing, radiant, and well-directed steeds of Dhvanya Lakṣmaṇya have come to me with the greatness of wealth, like cows entering the stall of the seer Saṃvaraṇa.
The ageless, heavenly *svadhā* follows the one who has no enemy, the wondrous one, according to his own measure.
Press the soma, cook the oblation for him who is borne by prayer; bestow further gifts upon him who is praised by many.
Maghavan, who filled his belly with Soma and rejoiced in the sweet juice;
when he, the wielder of great weapons, sent forth for the slaying of the beast a thousand-edged bolt, even as Uśanas directed it.
Whoever presses Soma for him—be it one who does so under the scorching heat or in the rainy season—that man indeed becomes radiant.
Śakra, the powerful one, drives away the malice of the one who extends his devotion; Maghavan, the wise friend, makes his body shine with splendor.
He whose father, whose mother, or whose brother Śakra has slain—he does not flee from him;
for he knows well how to make the one who offers gifts prosper, and as a source of wealth, he does not shrink from sin.
He desires neither five nor ten to begin [the rite]; he does not associate with one who does not press the Soma, even if that person is prosperous.
The shaker (Indra) conquers by this means or slays him; he bestows the pious man upon a stall full of cattle.

Possessing powerful jaws, he hurls his wheel into the encounter; turning away from the one who does not press the soma, he is the prosperer of the one who presses it. Indra, the terrifier and subduer of all, leads the Dāsa according to his will, as the Ārya.
He drives the Pani’s food together for plunder; he distributes excellent wealth to the donor.
Not even in a narrow pass does he hold back the many people who have provoked his might.
When Indra Maghavan perceived two wealthy men, each with a full host, contending for beautiful cattle, he made one his ally;
trembling, he released the cattle-herd for him with his warriors, shaking it down.

I praise Śatri, the son of Agniveśa, who possesses a thousand songs, O Agni—the peerless banner of the noble one. For him may the waters flow together in abundance; in him let there be powerful and brilliant dominion.
O Indra, bring us that most effective will of yours for our protection— that which overcomes the peoples, which wins booty, and which is invincible in battles.
O Indra, whatever four [treasures] you have, O hero, or whatever three there are,
or whatever [wealth] belongs to the five peoples— bring that aid well to us.
We invoke your most excellent aid, you who are most manly;
for you were born with manly impetuousness, O Indra, victorious with your helpers.
For you are a bull; you were born for the sake of bounty. Bullish is your strength; bold is your mind, O Indra, whose sovereign power is self-dependent and whose manly valor is all-conquering.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, O Lord of a hundred powers, O Master of might, come with all your chariots against that mortal who acts as an enemy.
O best slayer of Vṛtra, you indeed do the people who have trimmed the sacrificial grass invoke— the fierce one, the ancient one among many— for the winning of booty.
O Indra, protect our chariot— difficult to overcome, leading at the front in battles, racing alongside us in every contest for wealth, and striving for victory.
O Indra, come to our chariot with abundance; O most powerful one, may we win what is desirable. May we establish glory in heaven, and may we meditate upon praise in heaven.
May that Indra come, he who knows how to bestow treasures as a gift of riches;
like a thirsty bull wandering in the desert, let him drink the pressed soma-stalk.
O Hero, Lord of the Bay Steeds, may Soma rise upon your jaws and cheeks like [water] upon the back of a mountain.
O King, invoked by many, may we all rejoice with hymns of praise, urging you on as one urges swift horses.
O much-invoked wielder of the stone, my mind trembles like a revolving wheel from fear of destitution;
shall not the singer, O Maghavan, possessor of many riches and ever-increasing, praise you now from his chariot?
Like a pressing-stone, O Indra, this singer of yours raises his voice, aspiring to the lofty [song].
O Maghavan, bestow wealth with your left hand; O Lord of the Bay Steeds, bestow it with your right; do not be averse to us.
May the Bull Heaven cause you, the Bull, to grow; as a Bull, you are borne by your two Bulls, the bay steeds.
O Bull with the beautiful helmet, Bull of mighty will, Bull Wielder of the Thunderbolt, grant us a Bull’s portion in battle on your Bull-chariot.
He who, possessing steeds, bestowed two ruddy horses accompanied by three hundred [cows];
O Maruts, let all the peoples bow down before this youth Śrutaratha with reverent homage.
He vies with the radiance of the sun, offering oblations, his back anointed with ghee, moving with ease.
For him may the unceasing dawns shine forth, who says, "Let us press the Soma for Indra."
With the fire kindled and the sacrificial grass strewn, he shall win the forest; with the pressing-stones yoked and the Soma pressed, he shall sing his praise.
He for whom the pressing-stones speak with eager zeal—there the Adhvaryu priest has gone to the river with the oblation.
This bride comes seeking her husband, she who is carried as a vigorous queen; may his chariot win fame and let its roar resound, as it brings home many thousands of cattle.
That king does not tremble in whose presence Indra drinks the potent Soma accompanied by the cows;
he drives forth with his warriors, slays Vṛtra, dwells among the people, and prospers under the name of the fortunate one.
May he prosper in security and prevail in battle; may he conquer both armies when they meet.
He who has pressed the soma and offers it to Indra shall be dear to Sūrya and dear to Agni.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, the gift from your bounty is vast;
therefore, O Ruler of all people, O noble sovereign, bestow upon us glorious riches.
O most powerful Indra, when you bestow that glorious nourishment which is worthy of renown, it spreads abroad— most far-famed, golden-hued, and invincible.
O wielder of the stone, those vigorous ones of yours who are eager for the prize through their inspired thought—
both you gods, as lords of heaven and earth, rule for our protection.
And so, O Vṛtra-slayer, from whatever power of yours this may be, bring us manly strength; for you desire the welfare of men, bring it to us.
Now, O Śatakratu, through these aids of yours, may we abide in your protection;
O Indra, may we have good guardians, O Hero, may we have good guardians.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, whatever wonderful wealth there is that is bestowed by you,
O finder of riches, bring that bounty to us with both hands.
O Indra, bring that which you deem most excellent and celestial;
may we know it from you, as you bestow it in measureless abundance.
O wielder of the stone, with that renowned and lofty mind of yours which is intent on giving and attaining success, break open even the firmest obstacles to win us the prize of booty.
To Indra, the most bountiful among your wealthy patrons and the king of the peoples, I have offered many songs for his praise; he has been pleased by them.
To him, to Indra, this poetic word, this hymn, is to be recited;
for him, who is drawn by prayer, the Atris magnify their songs, the Atris adorn their songs.
Come hither; drink the Soma pressed by the stones, O Lord of Soma!
O Bull Indra, greatest slayer of Vṛtra, come with your bulls.
The pressing-stone is a bull, the exhilaration is a bull; this pressed Soma is a bull, O Indra, most slayer of Vṛtra, you who are a bull with your bulls.
As a bull, I call upon you, the bull, O wielder of the thunderbolt, with your wondrous aids;
O Indra, most excellent slayer of Vṛtra, come with your bull-like steeds.

The drinker of the dregs, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, the subduer of the swift, the impetuous king, the slayer of Vṛtra, the drinker of Soma— having yoked his two bay horses, may Indra come hither and exhilarate himself at the midday libation.
When Svarbhānu, the Asura, pierced you with darkness, O Sūrya,
all living beings looked on like one bewildered and ignorant of the way.
Then, O Indra, when you struck down the magical illusions of Svarbhānu as they rolled from heaven,
Atri found the sun hidden by the lawless darkness through the fourth sacred prayer.
Let not the malevolent one, out of envy and fear, swallow me up while I am here belonging to you. You are Mitra, whose wealth is truth; may you two, together with King Varuṇa, protect me.
Harnessing the pressing-stones, the priest Atri, serving and honoring the gods with his hymn while instructing them with reverence,
established the eye of the sun in heaven and dispelled the magical illusions of Svarbhānu.
The Asura Svarbhānu pierced the sun with darkness;
the Atris found him there, for no others were able.
Who indeed, O Mitra and Varuṇa, seeking the *ṛta*, would offer to you from the great heaven or from the earth?
Or in the seat of the *ṛta*, may you protect us; or for the sacrifice, grant us strengths like those who seek cattle.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Āyu, Indra, Ṛbhukṣan, and the Maruts be pleased with us;
or those who, being of one accord, offer well-fashioned praise and a hymn with salutations to the bounteous Rudra.

O Aśvins, I call you hither, you who are most swift to travel, in the flight of the wind and in the abundance of the chariot; or rather, bring forth this prayer to the Asura of heaven, as one brings food to a worthy sacrificer.
The conquering celestial one, Kaṇva the Hotṛ, Trita from heaven, Vāta, and Agni, acting in harmony;
Pūṣan, Bhaga, and all-nourishing Viśvabhojas—like those with the swiftest horses, they have come to the contest at the offering.
Bring forth your wealth with its harnessed horses; let the prayer be offered for the sake of finding riches and for protection.
May the priest of Auśija be very gracious through his rites—those rites which belong to you, O swift Maruts.

Bring forth Vāyu, who yokes his chariot, and the god, the inspired singer, to be praised with hymns. Seeking aid, you who follow the cosmic order, bring hither the bountiful and noble wives for our prayer here.
I approach you two with venerable invocations and with mighty, illuminating hymns from heaven—
the Dawn and Night, who, like those possessing all knowledge, bring the sacrifice to the mortal man.
I sing praise to you, the nourishing heroes; granting gifts, I honor Vāstoṣpati and Tvaṣṭṛ.
With homage, may the bountiful Dhīṣaṇā be well-disposed toward us; and for the sake of wealth, we seek the lords of the forest and the plants.
May the mountains be for our protection and extension—those who are well-guided like Vasu heroes.
May the praiseworthy Āptya, the worshipful one, ever increase our manly praise in his favor.
I have praised the embryo of the bull of the earth; Trita has extolled the Son of the Waters with a perfect hymn.
Agni, like a swift steed, is celebrated with vigorous powers; he of the flaming hair consumes the forests.
How shall we speak to the great Rudra? How to Bhaga, who is mindful of wealth?
May the waters and the plants protect us, as well as the sky, the forests, and the mountains with their tree-hair.
May the Lord of Strength hear our songs—he who is more swift than the wind, the vigorous one who moves all around.
May the waters hear us, bright as citadels, as they flow from the mountain that has been split open by the ladles.
Truly we know you to be great, O wondrous ones; we shall proclaim it as we receive what is desirable.
Even the well-winged birds do not descend upon the mortal who pursues them with weapons in his agitation.
I have proclaimed for the sake of the noble sacrificer the divine and earthly births and the waters;
may the heavens increase, may the songs with their bright peaks increase, and may the surging floods increase in power.
At every step may my old age be laid down, by Varūtrī or by Śakra with his protections.
May the great mother Rasā attend us, together with the patrons—she who is straight-handed and whose path is straight.

How may we worship with homage the bounteous givers, the Maruts who come swiftly at our invocation? O Maruts, you of great renown, at our invocation—let not Ahi Budhnya deliver us to harm; may he be a promoter of our prosperity.
Thus indeed, O gods, does the mortal man win you for the sake of offspring rich in cattle; thus, O gods, does the mortal man win you.
Herein, may Nirṛti swallow up even my old age, so that there may be a auspicious nourishment for this body.
O Gods, may we obtain from you that benevolent favor, strengthening nourishment, through the praise of the Cow, O Vasus.
May she, the bounteous and merciful Goddess, hastening toward us, come for our well-being.
May Iḷā, the mother of the herd, or Urvaśī together with the rivers, favor us; or may Urvaśī of the lofty heaven, being praised, cover us as she bestows the gift of the living one.
May he attend us with the nourishment of strengthening food.
May my most peaceful song with devotion now reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Bhaga, and Aditi.
May the Asura, whose path is unassailable, who is the source of joy, the fivefold invoker seated upon the speckled altar, hear us.
May Aditi accept my hymn of praise, as a mother her dear and very gracious son;
that beloved prayer which is ordained by the gods, and which brings delight to Mitra and Varuṇa.
Exalt the most wise among the sages; drench him with honey and clarified butter.
May that god Savitṛ bestow upon us brilliant treasures, already offered and set forth.

O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, unite us with a favorable mind, with cattle, and with wise patrons; unite us with well-being, with the sacred prayer ordained by the gods, and with the benevolent goodwill of the deities worthy of sacrifice.
May the god Bhaga, Savitṛ the apportioner of wealth, Indra the conqueror of Vṛtra and winner of riches,
Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, and Purandhi— may these immortal, swift ones protect us.
Let us proclaim the deeds of the one accompanied by the Maruts, the irresistible, the victorious, the undecaying.
Neither those of old, O Maghavan, nor those of later times, nor anyone of the present, have equaled your heroic power.
Praise Bṛhaspati, the first bestower of jewels, the winner of riches— he who, most beneficent to him who recites and praises, possessing abundant wealth, comes to the one who calls upon him.
O Bṛhaspati, through your protections, the liberal patrons are unharmed and possess excellent heroes;
those who are givers of horses, or givers of cattle, or givers of garments—they among them have abundant wealth and good fortune.
Make their wealth flow away—those who enjoy it without giving to us in return for our hymns.
At the impulse [of the gods], drive far from the sun those haters of prayer who increase while following contrary vows.
O Maruts, strike down with wheelless [missiles] that Rakṣas who shows contempt for the feast of the gods;
he who reviles the labor of one striving for you shall have his desires rendered empty, even though he exerts himself in sweat.
Praise him who possesses good arrows and a good bow, he who rules over every medicine.
Worship Rudra for his great benevolence; honor the divine Asura with prostrations.
May the householders, the active ones with skillful hands, the wives of the bull, the rivers fashioned by Vibhvan,
Sarasvatī, Bṛhaddivā, and Rākā— the radiant ones— grant us wide space, bestowing their favor.
I offer this newest, newly-born hymn of wisdom to the great one, the excellent refuge— he who,
fashioning forms within the womb of his daughter, brought all this into being for us.
O singer, may you now attain with your excellent praise the Lord of the *iḷā* offering, who thunders and roars— he who,
possessing clouds and possessing waters, sends forth lightning while drenching both heaven and earth.
May this hymn reach the Marut host, the sons of Rudra, the youthful ones.
Desire calls me for wealth; for my well-being, praise the tireless ones who have spotted deer as their steeds.
May this hymn of praise reach the earth, the mid-air, the trees, and the plants for the sake of wealth.
May every god be easy for me to invoke; may Mother Earth not hold us in ill-will.
O gods, may we abide in a wide space free from oppression.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid of the Aśvins, under their excellent guidance.
O Immortals, bring to us wealth, as well as heroic sons, and all auspicious blessings.
May the milch-cows, hastening toward their goal, come to us with milk and honey, never failing.
For great wealth, the inspired singer loudly calls upon the seven mighty ones who bring bliss.
With fair praise and with homage, I would turn hither Heaven and Earth, the unerring ones, for the sake of strength.
Father and Mother, sweet of speech and skillful-handed, may you two glorious ones protect us in every battle.
O Adhvaryus, having prepared the sweet juices, bring the lovely, bright [soma] to Vāyu.
Like our first Hotar, O God, drink of this honeyed [draught]; we have offered it to you for exhilaration.

The ten fingers and the two arms—the skillful preparers of the Soma—yoke the pressing-stone. The well-hoofed stalk, dwelling on the mountain, has yielded the bright, shimmering juice of the mead with its beautiful hands.
The Soma has been pressed for you who take delight in it, for the sake of wisdom, for skill, and for great exhilaration.
O Indra, being invoked, bring your two beloved bay steeds, well-yoked to the chariot, hitherward at the time of the rite.

O Agni, bring hither by the god-traversed paths the great Aramati, the divine lady who is in harmony with us, who is honored with homage and offered oblations— the lofty one who knows the cosmic order— for the exhilaration of the sweet mead.
Him whom the inspired poets anoint as if spreading him out, heating him with fire as if he were a fatty oblation—
the most beloved cauldron (gharma) has been set upon Agni, like a son in his father’s lap, performing the rite of Truth.
Let the great, lofty, and most auspicious song go forth like a messenger to invite the Aśvins.
O you who bring bliss, come hither on one chariot; come to the treasure, as the linchpin reaches the nave of the wheel.
I have proclaimed this word of homage to the most powerful Pūṣan and to Vāyu— the two who,
by their bounty, are the inspirers of our thoughts, and who themselves are the givers of wealth and of strength.

O Jātavedas, being invoked, bring hither all the Maruts by their names and by their forms; O all you Maruts, come to the sacrifice, to the songs and the beautiful hymn of the singer, with all your aids.
May Sarasvatī, the worshipful one, come from the high heaven and from the mountain to our sacrifice;
may the goddess, delighting in our call, dripping with clarity, and longing for us, graciously hear our effective speech.
Seat the ordainer, the blue-backed, the great Bṛhaspati, in his dwelling. Let us honor him who shines in his own place within the house—the golden-hued, the ruddy one.
May the sustainer from the high heaven, bestowing gifts, come hither with all his protections when invoked—
the bull who clothes himself in the wives and the plants, the unfailing one with triple-horns, the bestower of vital strength.

To the bright one in the highest station of his mother, the active ones, full of praise and eloquent, have come. With reverence, offering oblations, they purify the child for his gracious favor, as Āyus do for their own dwelling.
Great vital power belongs to you, O great Agni; those who have grown old through devotion attend upon you in pairs.
May every god be easy for me to invoke; may Mother Earth not hold us in ill-will.
O gods, may we abide in a wide space free from oppression.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid and excellent guidance of the Aśvins.
O Immortals, bring to us wealth, heroic sons, and all auspicious fortunes.
As of old, as before, as always, and even so now, [we invoke] him who sits upon the sacrificial grass, the finder of heaven, the pre-eminent one;
with our song we milk from him the facing-inward stronghold—the swift, victorious one—in whom you grow strong.
For the sake of glory, those [rays] of the upper sun are beautiful to behold; shining forth, you do not urge on the quarters of heaven.
You are a good guardian, O wise one, not to be deceived; beyond all illusions, your name is established in the *ṛta*.
The oblation follows the steed; he is both the companion and the bestower, the Hotar-priest whose path is unharmed and who brings strength.
Striding along the sacrificial grass, the bull, the infant, the youth, and the ageless one has been placed in the midst of the spreading branches.

These well-yoked [mares] go forward on their course for the sacrifice; for him over there, the twin sisters flow downward, increasing the cosmic order (*ṛta*). With reins that are easy to control and all-commanding, Krivi steals away their names in the descent.
Moving to and fro among the trees, seizing the pressed juice, you of beautiful form shine within the vessels that contain the thought;
O singer of straight hymns, you are resplendent amidst the calls for the libation. Increase in strength at the sacrifice, O living one, as you approach your consorts.
Just as he was seen, so is he described; they have established him with a successful reflection within the waters.
Grant us great, wide space and vast dominion—mighty, heroic, and unshakable strength.
Whether he is unmarried or has a wife, Sūrya the sage, with a mind intent on battle, overcomes his rivals;
may he, whose wealth is his own, grant us a shelter that protects our home from all sides against the scorcher.
By the signal of this striving one, he moves toward the greater [power], in which your name, O Rishi-lord, resides.
In whatever [vessel] it is placed, he finds it through his skillful work; and he who carries it himself shall make it ready.
The foremost of these has descended into the ocean; the libation in which she is extended is not harmed.
Herein the heart of the impetuous one trembles, where the hymn exists that is bound to the purified Soma.
For he, through the intentions of Kṣatra Manasa, of Evāvada, of Yajata,
and of Sadhri— of Avatsāra— we shall win by means of our delights the most powerful strength, which is to be attained even by the wise.
The falcon is their Aditi; the exhilaration of Viśvavāra, the worshipful and wondrous one, is like a girth-belt.
They strive together to go toward one another; they know the horn, your drink that surrounds them.
May the ever-generous Yajata slay the enemies; may Bāhuvṛkta, Śrutavid, and Tarya be with you.
He attains both boons and shines forth when he joins his troop with those who are well-prepared for the journey.
The sustainer of the pressed juice, the lord of the virtuous, he is the udder of all prayers and the vessel that draws them forth.
Bringing the milk of the milch-cows, he has established the flavorful draught; reciting the hymns, he masters it, for he does not sleep.
The Ṛg-verses long for him who is awake; the Sāman-chants go to him who is awake.
To him who is awake, this Soma says: "I am yours, dwelling at home in your friendship."
Agni is awake; the *ṛc*s long for him. Agni is awake; the *sāmans* go toward him.
Agni is awake; to him this Soma says: "I am yours, dwelling at home in your friendship."

Finding the heaven, they opened the mountain with hymns; the singers went forth to the approaching Dawn. The enclosure was thrown open, the light ascended; O God, you have flung wide the doors for mankind.
Sūrya has sent forth his splendor like a radiance; the Mother of the Cows, knowing the way, has come from the wide space.
The rivers with desert-like banks have their waves swelling; the sky is made firm like a well-erected pillar.
For this hymn of praise, the child of the mountain [has come] for the sake of the ancient birth of the great ones;
the mountain has opened wide, heaven has been perfected, and those who seek to win him over have exhausted the earth.
With hymns and words pleasing to the gods, I shall now invoke Indra and Agni for your protection;
for with chants, the seers of skillful sacrifice, seeking to win them over, worship the Maruts.
Come now, let us today be of pure mind; let us drive far away misfortune to a wider space.
Let us cast our enemies far into the distance, and let us go forward toward the sacrificer.
O friends, let us perform this prayer by which the Mother opened the stall of the cow;
by which Manu conquered Viśiśipra, and by which the merchant Vaṅku obtained the treasure.
There the pressing-stone, guided by hands, roared; thereby the Navagvas sang for ten months.
Saramā, going according to the *ṛta*, found the cows; Aṅgiras made all things true.

When at the dawning of this majestic goddess, all the Aṅgirases together shouted for joy with their cattle, their fountain was found in the highest dwelling-place; by the path of Eternal Order, Saramā discovered the cows.

May Sūrya come with his seven horses to the field that extends over the wide earth on his long journey. May the swift falcon fly toward the soma-plant; may the youthful sage shine brightly as he goes among the cattle.
Sūrya has ascended to the bright ocean when he has yoked his tawny, straight-backed steeds.
As wise men steer a ship through the water, so did they lead him; the waters, hearing him, stood still before him.
I place my prayer for you among the waters, seeking the light of heaven—by which the Navagvas crossed over the ten months.
Through this prayer may we have the gods as our guardians; through this prayer may we overcome distress.
Like a wise horse, I have yoked myself of my own accord to the pole; I bear that which carries across and seeks aid.
I do not desire to unyoke from this, nor to turn back again; may the wise one who goes before us lead us straight upon the path.
O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and gods, grant us strength, O Maruts and Viṣṇu!
May both the Nāsatyas, Rudra, the divine wives, Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Sarasvatī be pleased.
I invoke Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sun, Earth, Heaven, the Maruts, and the Mountains;
I call upon Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Bhaga, Śaṃsa, and Savitṛ for our protection.
May Viṣṇu and Vāta grant us freedom from harm; may Draviṇodas and Soma bring us joy. May the Ṛbhus, the Aśvins for our wealth, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Vibhvan likewise take heed of us.
And may that host of Maruts come to us, dwelling in heaven, the worshipful ones, to sit upon the sacred grass;
may Bṛhaspati and Pūṣan grant us protection, and may Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us a secure refuge.
And may those mountains be well-praised for us, and the rivers, shining brightly, be our protection.
May Bhaga, the distributor, come with power and aid; may the far-reaching Aditi hear my call.

May the longing wives of the gods protect us; may they aid us for the sake of offspring and for the winning of booty. Those who belong to the earth and those who are in the domain of the waters—may those goddesses, who are easily invoked, grant us protection.
And may the divine wives, the consorts of the gods—Indrāṇī, Agnāyī, and Aśvinī the queen—come hither;
may Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us; may the goddesses come, they who are the season of women.

Setting forth, she goes from heaven, speaking as the great mother awakening her daughter; the youthful woman, seeking to win favor, calls out loudly to the fathers at their seat with inspired thought.
Swift-moving, hastening toward those waters, they have taken their stand at the navel of immortality;
boundless and vast, their paths go all around heaven and earth on every side.
The bull, the ocean, the ruddy one, the fair-winged bird, has entered the womb of the ancient father.
Placed in the midst of heaven like a speckled stone, he has strode forth; he guards the two ends of the region.
Four bear him up, seeking security; ten suckle the embryo for its movement.
His supreme cows, possessing a triple nature, traverse the ends of heaven in an instant.
O people, this is that wondrous form and secret speech which the rivers and the waters observe;
for two others, born here and there, twin and kinsmen, support him apart from his mother.
For him they extend their prayers and perform their works; as mothers weave garments for their son, the joyful bulls, sporting at the sprinkling, go toward the brides along the path of heaven.
May that be so, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may that be so, O Agni. May this be auspicious and healing for us, may this recitation be successful.
May we attain a firm footing and a secure standing. Homage to the great Heaven, the dwelling place!
When shall we meditate upon our own dear dwelling, great with its own dominion and its own glory—
when the creative power, choosing the waters from within the cloud-like, unfailing mid-air, spreads them out?
They have stretched out the path that nourishes heroes, across the entire expanse with a single course.
The person devoted to the gods drives away the waters behind him and pushes them forward with those already passed.
With these pressing-stones, throughout the days and nights, he hurls the most excellent thunderbolt at the wielder of magic.
He who, while moving about in his own abode, brings together a hundred [days] or lets them pass away, turning the days both together and apart.
I have beheld his onset like the edge of an axe; I have looked upon his countenance that we may enjoy his wondrous form.
When he bestows treasure upon the people who call him to battle, it is as if he were providing a dwelling full of nourishment.
With his tongue, the four-faced one reaches out, clothed in beauty; Varuṇa, striving for the pious man, bestows his favor.
We do not know him in his human form, from whence Bhaga and Savitṛ grant what is desirable.
Today I seek for you the god Savitṛ and Bhaga, who distributes wealth to mankind.
O Aśvins, heroes of many enjoyments, may I turn you both hither day by day, seeking your friendship.
Knowing the departure of the Asura, honor the god Savitṛ with hymns;
let him who understands address him with reverence, [praising] the eldest and the one who distributes wealth to mankind.
To the non-giver he grants desirable boons: Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aditi, and Dawn appear at daybreak;
Indra, Viṣṇu, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—these wondrous ones have generated auspicious days.
May the invincible Savitṛ grant us that protection; may the life-sustaining rivers follow it.
When I, as the Hotṛ of the sacrifice, address this prayer, may we become masters of wealth, rich in booty.

Those who offer such homage to the Vasus, and those who address Mitra and Varuṇa with hymns of praise—let the monstrous vanish, let them make wide room; through the grace of Heaven and Earth, may we rejoice.
May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader;
everyone strives for wealth, and may he choose glory so that he may prosper.
O God, those who are yours, O Leader, and those who follow this teaching— may we, through our companionship, be united with wealth and with those worthy of fellowship.
Therefore, honor our men who are guests, and therefore honor our wives;
may the Dispeller drive far away every enemy who stands upon our path.
Where the bearer has been urged forward like a beast of the trough,
he who is mindful of men, whose home is heroes— he wins the floods like a steady thinker.
O God, this leader of yours, the lord of the chariot, is wealth for our well-being;
we meditate upon him who is auspicious for riches and auspicious for prosperity—him whom we praise with food, him whom we praise as a god.
O Agni, come with all the helpful gods for the drinking of the pressed juice,
for the giving of the oblation to the gods.
O you whose thoughts are fixed on the Eternal Order, whose laws are truth, come to the sacrifice;
drink with the tongue of Agni.
O wise one, come with the wise singers who travel at dawn, O truthful one, together with the gods for the drinking of the Soma.
This Soma, pressed in the mortar, is poured into the vessel, dear to Indra and Vāyu.
O Vāyu, come for the feast, graciously accepting the gift of the oblation;
drink of the pressed juice for our refreshment.
O Indra and Vāyu, you two deserve the drinking of these pressed juices;
O stainless ones, enjoy them along with the offerings.
The Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for Indra and Vāyu;
like rivers flowing down a slope, they go toward the offering.
In harmony with all the gods, in harmony with the Aśvins and with Uṣas, come, O Agni; rejoice in the pressed juice as you did at Atri’s dwelling.
In harmony with Mitra and Varuṇa, in harmony with Soma and Viṣṇu, come, O Agni; rejoice in the pressed juice as you did for Atri.
In harmony with the Ādityas and the Vasus, in harmony with Indra and Vāyu, come hither, O Agni; rejoice in the pressed juice as you did for Atri.
May the Aśvins and Bhaga grant us well-being; may the goddess Aditi, who is free from enemies, grant us well-being.
May Pūṣan, the Asura, bestow well-being upon us; may Heaven and Earth, with their gracious intent, grant us well-being.
For our well-being, let us address Vāyu; for our well-being, Soma, who is the lord of the world;
Bṛhaspati with his entire host for our well-being; may the Ādityas be for our well-being.
