May all the gods today grant us well-being; may Agni Vaiśvānara, the Vasu, grant us well-being.
May the divine Ṛbhus protect us for our well-being; may Rudra preserve us from distress.
May there be well-being, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may there be well-being, O wealthy Pathyā.
May Indra and Agni grant us well-being; O Aditi, bestow well-being upon us.
May we follow the path with well-being, like the sun and the moon;
may we come together again with one who gives, who does not strike, and who knows.
O Śyāvāśva, sing boldly with the Maruts who are rich in hymns— those worshipful ones who, according to their wont, rejoice in blameless glory.
For they are the friends of steadfast power; with boldness, they protect all those who are impetuous on their journey by their own selves.
Like rushing bulls, they leap across the nights;
then we celebrate the greatness of the Maruts in heaven and upon the earth.
Upon the Maruts let us boldly place our hymn and sacrifice—
those who protect every human generation from harm throughout their mortal lives.
To those Maruts, the worthy ones who bestow excellent gifts, heroes of perfect strength— to them, the worshipful ones of heaven, I sing forth this sacrifice.
With their golden ornaments and with their weapons, the lofty heroes have hurled forth their spears;
following after these Maruts, who are like laughing lightnings, the splendor of heaven has risen by its own power.
Those who have grown great upon the earth, those who are in the wide mid-air,
or in the gathering place of the rivers, or in the assembly of the great heaven—
Praise the host of Maruts, truly powerful and skillful;
for indeed, those heroes, eager for glory, have themselves yoked their swift steeds.
And indeed, on the Paruṣṇī river, your pure ones wore woolen garments;
and with the tires of their chariots, they split the mountain by their might.
The paths that come from afar, those that go astray, those within the path, and those that follow the path—
with these names for me, they offer the sacrifice as a wide expanse.
Then the men harness themselves; then the teams of horses are harnessed.
Then, O Pārāvatas, your wondrous forms are visible to the eye.
Chanting hymns and seeking the waters, the singers have danced toward the spring;
they were like thieves to me, helpers appearing for a brilliant sight.
Those who are lofty, whose spears are like lightning, who are seers and wise ordainers—
to that host of Maruts, O seer, pay homage and delight them with your song.
O Rishi, come toward the host of Maruts with gifts, as a young woman approaches her friend;
or rather, O bold ones, impelled by our prayers, hasten hither from heaven with your might.
Now, mindful of these [deeds], may he not fail to lead us toward the gods; may he be united with the liberal patrons who are renowned for their journeys and adorned with ornaments.
The wise ones who, in their desire for kinship, have proclaimed for me the cow; they have proclaimed Pṛśni as the mother.
And then the skillful ones have proclaimed the impetuous Rudra as the father.
Seven times seven powerful ones have each given me a hundred gifts. On the Yamunā, I celebrate the famous bounty of cattle; I celebrate the bounty of horses.
Who knows their birth, or who was formerly in the favor of the Maruts,
when they yoked their spotted deer?
Who has heard of them as they stood upon their chariots, or how they went? To which liberal patron did the friendly rains flow together with the *iḷā* offerings?
They have told this to me, those who have come hither with their radiant steeds in exhilaration: "Praise these blameless heroes, O men, as you behold them."
Those who possess their own luster in their ointments, or in their axes, in their garlands, in their golden ornaments, and in their rings;
those who are upon their chariots and in their bows.
O Maruts, givers of quickening rain, I set my heart on your chariots for joy,
like the rains coming from the heavens.
The men of liberal gifts have shaken down from heaven the treasure-chest for the donor;
they release Parjanya over the two worlds, and the rains flow across the desert wastes.
Breaking through the mist with their flood, the rivers have rushed forth into the mid-air like milch-cows;
they spread out like swift horses at the unyoking of their paths when the bright streams flow asunder.
Come hither, O Maruts, from heaven, from the intermediate space, and from the earth;
do not remain in the far distance.
May the Rasā, Anitabhā, Kubhā, and Krumu not detain you; may the Sindhu not hold you back.
May the turbid Sarayu not stand in your way; let your favor be with us alone.
That host of yours, the brilliant Marut host of chariots, the newest of them—
after it the rains follow.
With excellent praises and with our prayers, may we follow after each of their hosts, each of their troops, and each of their companies.
To whom today have they gone forth— with their well-formed bodies and offerings presented—
to this course of yours, O Maruts?
With that [wealth] by which you bring inexhaustible seed-grain for our children and descendants— grant us that bounty for which we pray to you, and all-encompassing prosperity.
May we pass beyond reproach through blessings, leaving behind blame and hostilities;
having rained down peace and well-being, O Maruts, may we be with you, like the waters and the healing medicine of the dawn.
O Maruts, that mortal man shall be a good king, possessed of noble sons and great renown, whom you protect; may we be such as he.
Praise the liberal patrons on the journey of this singer, rejoicing like cattle in a pasture;
call after them with song like old friends, and celebrate those who desire you.
To the host of Maruts, self-luminous and shaking the mountains, I offer this speech.
To those who praise the *gharma* oblation, who sacrifice upon the back of heaven, and whose glory is radiant—sing of their great manly power!
O Maruts, your powerful, water-seeking, strength-increasing, horse-yoked bands move all around;
they discharge lightning, Trita roars, and the waters resound as they flow around the woods.

The Maruts, heroes of lightning-splendor, whose darts are like stones, who flash with the fury of the wind, shakers of mountains; though they move with the clouds, they are suddenly covered in hail, roaring with thunder, impetuous and of uplifted might.
O Rudras, you who are skillful and shakers of all things, you traverse the nights and the days; you traverse the mid-air and the regions of space.
O Maruts, just as one crosses over fields with a boat, you pass through difficult terrains, yet you are never harmed.
That heroic power of yours, O Maruts, and that greatness of yours has extended far, like the sun across its course.
Like these [horses] in their journey, you whose splendor is ungraspable, when you cast down the mountain for him who gives no horses.

The host of Maruts shone forth when you, O wise ones, stripped the tree like a caterpillar from the sap. Now, being of one mind, lead our devotion along an easy path, as one leads the eye toward its goal.

O Maruts, he whom you protect—whether he be a seer or a king—is not conquered, nor is he slain; he does not fail, he is not shaken, and he does not come to harm. Neither his wealth nor his aids ever diminish.
Like men who possess teams of horses and conquer the hosts, like Aryaman, the Maruts carry water-skins;
when they roar with their might, they fill the spring, and they drench the earth with the juice of honey.
This earth is full of slopes for the Maruts; the sky becomes full of slopes for those who advance.
The paths of the mid-air are full of slopes, and the mountains, which grant life-sustaining gifts, are full of slopes.
O Maruts, sharers of the spoils, heroes of heaven, you who rejoice at the rising of the sun, O men of the sky—your horses do not falter as they gallop; instantly you reach the end of this journey.
Upon your shoulders are spears, on your feet rings, golden ornaments on your chests, O Maruts, and splendors upon your chariot;
lightning-flashes with the brilliance of fire are in your hands, and golden helmets are spread upon your heads.
O Maruts, you shake down from that firmament—the ungraspable, radiant heaven—its bright fruit for the noble one.
The enclosures close in when they blaze forth; seeking the Truth, they raise a far-reaching shout.
O wise Maruts, may we be the masters of chariots of wealth full of vigor given by you;
O Maruts, bestow upon us thousandfold riches that do not fail, like Tiṣya from the sky.
O Maruts, you grant wealth consisting of desirable heroes; you protect the seer who is inspired by the Sāman.
You bestow a swift horse and booty upon the Bharata; you establish a king who is full of obedience.

O you who are swift to help, I beg that wealth from you by which we may extend ourselves over men like the sun; O Maruts, graciously accept this word of mine, through the power of which we may cross over a hundred winters.
The Maruts, eager for sacrifice, with gleaming spears and golden breastplates, have assumed great vigor;
they hasten with well-governed, swift horses, and as they go toward splendor, their chariots follow.
You yourselves assume power, as you know how; O great ones, you rule widely over the vast expanse.
They have measured out the mid-air with their might; as they go forth in splendor, their chariots have rolled along.
Born together, well-being-bringers, grown up together, these heroes have increased further for the sake of glory;
like the radiant rays of the sun, their chariots have turned to follow them as they go in splendor.
O Maruts, your greatness is worthy of adoration; it is worthy of being beheld, like the very sight of the sun.
Furthermore, establish us in immortality. As they went forth in splendor, their chariots followed.
O Maruts, you raise the rain from the ocean; you, O possessors of moisture, cause the rain to fall.
Your milch-cows, O wonder-workers, never fail; as you go forth in splendor, your chariots have rolled along.
When you have yoked the spotted mares to the poles of the horses and have put on your golden mantles, O Maruts, you scatter all rivals; when they go forth in splendor, their chariots roll along.
Neither mountains nor rivers can obstruct you where you have resolved to go, O Maruts;
even heaven and earth you pass around, for as you go forth in splendor, your chariots have rolled along.

O Maruts, whatever is ancient and whatever is new, whatever is spoken, O Vasus, and whatever is recited—of all that you are the witnesses; as they go toward splendor, their chariots have turned to follow.
Be gracious to us, O Maruts; do not strike us down. Extend to us manifold protection.
Take heed of our hymn and of our friendship. As they go forth in splendor, their chariots have turned hither.
O Maruts, being praised, lead us toward greater wealth and deliver us from distress;
O holy ones, enjoy our offering of oblations, and may we be masters of riches.
O Agni, [bring] the bold host, adorned with golden ornaments and decorations;
today I call down the folk of the Maruts even from the luminous realm of heaven.
Just as you intend in your heart, so have my prayers reached you;
strengthen those of fearsome appearance who have come most closely to your invocations.
Like a bountiful woman, the earth, struck down, comes toward us exulting;
O Maruts, your impetuous power is like a fierce bear, like a wild bull, terrifying.
Those who by their might flow forth at will like oxen difficult to yoke—
they cause even the heavenly stone, the rocky mountain, to tremble with their journeys.
Arise now with the hymns of these who have been sprinkled together;
I call upon the most abundant and unprecedented host of Maruts, like a release of cattle.
Yoke the two ruddy mares to the chariot; yoke the two red horses to the chariots.
Yoke the two swift bay steeds to the pole to draw, the best at drawing to the pole.
And may that ruddy steed, loud-sounding and worthy of praise, be established here as beautiful to behold.
O Maruts, let him not cause delay for you on your journeys; urge him forward upon your chariots.
We now invoke the Marut’s chariot, which seeks renown—
the chariot upon which Rodasī stands together with the Maruts, bringing forth delightful things.
I invoke that host of yours, brilliant on chariots, impetuous, and worthy of praise—
the host in which the well-born, fortunate, and bountiful goddess exults together with the Maruts.
O Rudras, accompanied by Indra and acting in harmony, come on your golden chariots for our well-being.
This prayer of ours is offered to you with delight, like a spring of water from heaven to one who thirsts for it.
Armed with axes and spears, wise, with good bows, arrows, and quivers;
with fine horses and excellent chariots, O sons of Pṛśni, you are well-armed—O Maruts, go forth for glory!
You shake the sky and the mountains to bestow wealth upon the donor; out of fear of your march, the forests bow down before you.
O sons of Pṛśni, you stir up the earth when you, the fierce ones, have harnessed your spotted deer for glory.
The Maruts, flashing like the wind, clothed in rain, are as perfectly alike as twins and well-adorned;
with tawny horses and ruddy steeds, they are stainless, impetuous, and in their greatness as vast as the sky.

Abounding in drops, adorned with ornaments, bounteous givers, brilliant in appearance, and possessing inexhaustible wealth— well-born by birth, with golden plates upon their breasts, these hymns of heaven have attained immortality as their name.

Spears are upon your shoulders, O Maruts; together, vigor is placed in your arms and strength in your hands. Manly power is in your heads, weapons upon your chariots, and all your splendor is adorned upon your bodies.
O Maruts, grant us wealth consisting of cattle, horses, chariots, and brave sons, as well as glittering riches;
O sons of Rudra, bestow upon us high renown, and may I enjoy your divine protection.
Come hither, O heroes, O Maruts, be gracious to us—you who possess abundant wealth, are immortal, and know the cosmic order;
you who hear the truth, are sages, youthful, possessing lofty mountains, and increasing with great strength.
Now indeed I praise that powerful host of theirs, the Marut troop of the most recent [gods],
who drive with swift horses like stormy winds and who, as self-ruling kings, lord it over immortality.
The brilliant host, powerful, with devouring hands, whose law is to shake, full of magic power, bountiful— those who bring bliss,
immeasurable in their greatness, O sage, praise those men of abundant wealth!
May your water-bearing steeds come today, all you Maruts who impel the rain.
O Maruts, this fire which has been kindled—take pleasure in it, O youthful seers!

O worshipful Maruts, you generate for the people a vigorous king, fashioned by Vibhvan; from you comes the hand-to-hand fighter incited by his arm, and from you, O Maruts, he who possesses good horses and heroic sons.
Like spokes, they are without end; like days, they are born forth again and again, not deficient in their greatness.
The sons of Pṛśni, the most excellent and most powerful, the Maruts, have united themselves by their own thought.
When you have set forth with your spotted deer as horses, O Maruts, on chariots with strong fellies—
the waters are stirred, the forests give way, and let the bull of heaven, the sun, roar down from above.

Even the earth itself has spread wide at their coming; they have brought forth their own power like a husband his seed. For they have yoked the winds as horses to the pole; the sons of Rudra have turned their sweat into rain.

O heroes, O Maruts, have mercy on us! You who possess abundant wealth, you immortals who know the cosmic order (*ṛta*), you who hear the truth, you sages, young men, dwelling on lofty mountains and growing great—[be gracious to us].
They have stirred themselves for you to grant us prosperity; let me sing praise to Heaven and offer the sacred Law (*ṛta*) to Earth.
They bathe their horses and hasten across the mid-air; they spread their own radiance with surging waves.
The earth trembles from fear of them; like a full ship, she quivers as she moves along.
Those heroes, visible from afar, who make themselves known by their approaches, have striven within the great assembly.
Like the preeminent horns of bulls for the sake of beauty, like the eye of the sun at the unfolding of the mid-world;
you are as beautiful as well-formed horses, and like young men, O heroes, you take thought for glory.
Who could reach the greatness of you, the great ones? Who, O Maruts, your poetic wisdom, and who your manly deeds?
You indeed cause the earth to tremble like a particle of dust when you bring forth [your power] to grant us prosperity.
Like ruddy horses of the same kin, like heroes eager for combat, they have indeed fought forward;
like well-grown youths, these men have grown strong, and with their rains they diminish the eye of the sun.
They have no eldest, no youngest, and no middle; these breakers-forth have grown great through their majesty.
Well-born by birth, sons of Pṛśni, youths of heaven, come hither toward us!
Like birds that fly in rows by their might from the ridges of the vast heaven,
their horses— both kinds, as they know— have caused the springs of the mountain to flow forth.
May Dyaus Aditi low for our enjoyment; may the Dawns, wondrous in their gifts, strive together.
O Seer, these Maruts of Rudra, being praised, have caused the celestial vessel to pour forth.
I praise Agni, the self-luminous, with prostrations; seated here, may he discern our deed.
Like chariots seeking booty, I bring forth my offering; may I successfully complete this hymn of praise to the Maruts, moving from left to right.

The Rudras, the Maruts, who have mounted their famous spotted deer and their easy-gliding chariots—out of fear of you, O fierce ones, even the forests bow down; even the earth trembles, and even the mountain quakes.
Even the mountain, though greatly grown, was afraid; even the ridge of heaven trembled at your roar.
When you play, O Maruts, armed with spears, you rush together like waters.
Like prize-winning stallions, they have adorned their bodies with gold and their own inherent powers;
for the sake of glory, these most excellent and mighty ones have fully displayed their splendors upon their chariots and their persons.
Among these brothers, there is neither eldest nor youngest; they have grown together for good fortune.
Their father is the youthful Rudra, skillful in his work; Pṛśni is their well-yielding cow, bringing fair days to the Maruts.
Whether you, O bountiful Maruts, dwell in the highest, the middle, or even the lowest heaven,
therefore, O Rudras, and you, O Agni, take note of this oblation which we sacrifice here.
When you, O Maruts, possessors of all wealth, together with Agni, carry [the oblation] from the highest ridge of heaven by means of your heights—
then, being exhilarated, you roarers who destroy the enemy, bestow wealth upon the sacrificer who presses the Soma.

O Agni Vaiśvānara, rejoicing with the Maruts— the radiant ones who sing hymns, who possess the glory of their hosts, the purifying, all-impelling, and life-sustaining ones— drink the Soma together with them,
united from of old by our banner of light.
Who are you, O men, the most excellent ones, who have come one by one from the furthest distance?
Where are your horses, where are your reins? How did you succeed, how did you go? A seat is upon your back; the yoke is upon your nostrils.
A goad is upon their hindquarters; the men have spread their thighs apart like women for the procreation of sons.
Go forth, O heroes, O young men of auspicious birth,
so that you may be heated by the fire.
May she grant cattle consisting of horses and kine, numbering a hundred sheep,
to the hero praised by Śyāvāśva, whom she strengthened with her arms.
Moreover, a woman who is more modest becomes even better than a man who is godless and ungenerous.
She who discerns the exhausted, the thirsty, and the desiring,
turns her mind toward the gods.
And indeed, there is no one who is not praised; I call him a man, even if he be a Pani.
He is equal [to others] in the matter of the prize to be won in battle.
And the young woman, having been exhilarated, cleared the path for Śyāva;
the two ruddy steeds were yoked for Purumīḷha, the inspired singer of far-reaching fame.
He who, like Vaidadaśvi, gave me a hundred cows,
like Taranta with his great bounty.
Those who carry him with swift steeds, drinking the intoxicating honey-sweet mead,
have here acquired glorious renown.
They on whose chariots the two worlds shine with splendor,
like a golden ornament high in the sky.
That youthful host of Maruts, with its brilliant chariot, is blameless, seeking splendor, and irresistible.
Who indeed truly knows of these, where the shakers rejoice—
those born of Truth, stainless?
O you who are eager for praise, you are the leaders of the mortal man through this very prayer;
you are the hearers at the calls of the journey.
O destroyers of enemies, you who are worthy of sacrifice, turn toward us those desirable riches that are many and most brilliant.
O Night, goddess, carry away this hymn of mine to Dārbhya Ūrmya, like a charioteer carrying his songs.
And let him say this for me when the soma has been pressed at the dwelling of Rathavīti:
"My desire does not depart."
This Maghavan, Rathavīti, dwells among the cattle-rich [regions],
taking refuge in the mountains.
By the Truth is your firm Truth covered, where they unyoke the horses of the Sun;
there, ten hundred stand together—I have seen that one supreme form among the gods.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, that is truly your greatness: the waters, standing still, have been milked day by day. You cause all the streams of the stall to swell; for you alone has the single stone rolled onward.
O kings Mitra and Varuṇa, by your greatness you have supported both the earth and the sky;
cause the plants to flourish, make the cows swell with milk, and pour down rain, O you whose gifts are quickening.
May your well-yoked horses with their reins bring you hither; may they come toward us.
A coating of clarified butter follows you; from of old, the rivers flow for you.
Increasing the far-reaching, renowned wisdom, guarding it as one protects the sacrificial grass with a *yajus* formula,
you two— reverent and firm in resolve— sit upon the throne within the waters, O Mitra and Varuṇa.

With hands that bear no blood, you protect the doer of good deeds; O Varuṇa and Iḷā, whomsoever you two shield within your care, O Kings who never falter in your sovereignty, you two together uphold the dominion upon a thousand pillars.
With golden girdle and iron pillar, it shines forth like a whip for the horses in heaven; may we win of the honeyed [Soma] placed upon the high seat, as if fixed in a fertile field or a rich soil.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, you ascend the golden-hued seat at the dawning of the dawn, with its bronze pillars at the rising of the sun; from there, you behold both Aditi and Diti.
O bounteous guardians of the world, Mitra and Varuna, with that most ample, flawless protection which none can pierce, favor us; thus, as we strive for victory, may we be victorious.
O guardians of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), you whose laws are truth, you mount your chariot in the highest heaven.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, for whomever you provide protection here, for him the rain of heaven pours forth sweetness.
As sovereign lords you rule over this world, O Mitra and Varuṇa, who behold the light in the assembly.
We pray for your rain, your bounty, and immortality; the thunderers move across heaven and earth.
Sovereign kings, fierce bulls, lords of heaven and of earth, Mitra and Varuṇa, you who are far-seeing;
with wondrous clouds you attend the roar, and by the creative power (*māyā*) of the Asura, you cause the sky to rain.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, your wondrous power rests in heaven; the sun moves as a brilliant light, a marvelous weapon.
You conceal him in the sky with cloud and rain; O Parjanya, honey-sweet drops surge forth.

The Maruts harness their easy chariot for glory, like a hero in the search for cattle, O Mitra and Varuṇa. The thundering clouds traverse the bright regions; O sovereign kings, sprinkle us with the milk of heaven.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, Parjanya speaks a word full of nourishment, wondrous and brilliant with power. The Maruts clothe themselves in clouds through their great skill; cause the ruddy, stainless heaven to rain down.
By the Law, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who are wise, you guard the sacred ordinances through the creative power of the Asura.
By the Eternal Order you rule over the entire world; you have placed the sun in heaven as a wondrous chariot.
We invoke Varuṇa, the destroyer of enemies, and Mitra with a hymn for you;
like two who have gone around a pen with their arms, they have reached the sun-like hero.
Stretch out those two arms with benevolence toward this singer who praises you; for your auspicious and venerable nature is proclaimed throughout all lands.
If now I should attain that goal, may I go by the path of Mitra; in the protection of this beloved one, who does no harm, they have ever remained.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we establish for you through this hymn that which is worthy of praise,
so that it may prevail in the dwelling of the wealthy patrons and among those who offer songs of praise.
May Mitra and Varuṇa come to us with their radiant splendors to our common dwelling, in our own home, for the prosperity of the wealthy patrons and of our friends.
O Varuṇa, you two uphold for us among those [people] a great dominion;
make wide room for us for the winning of booty, for wealth, and for well-being.
O worshipful ones, while the dawn breaks upon the divine realm where the cattle are radiant,
come hither on foot like those who carry the pressed Soma with their hands— O heroes, you who support Arcanānas!
He who has perceived it is truly wise; let him speak for us among the gods—Varuṇa, the visible one, or Mitra—whoever wins over our songs of praise.
For they are two kings of most excellent luster, whose fame is heard most far; they are the lords of the good, increasers of *ṛta*, and observers of *ṛta* among every people.
Approaching you both for protection, I invoke you first with these words; may we, possessing good horses, through your wise guidance, prevail in the winning of spoils.
Mitra wins a wide path even from distress for his dwelling;
for the favor of Mitra, who overcomes all, belongs to the one who serves him.
May we abide in the most extensive protection of Mitra; through your aid, O Varuṇa, may we be entirely free from distress, sharing in your abundance.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two urge this people together and lead them on;
do not overlook the patrons, nor us sages; protect us in your guardianship.
O mortal, being mindful, bring hither the two gods of noble will who destroy the foe;
let him offer to Varuṇa, whose form is truth, for great enjoyment.
For they have attained unswerving dominion and perfect divine power;
and like a law for mankind, the beautiful light has been established like the sun.
In this pursuit of yours, we— those who offer oblations— firmly meditate upon your broad pasture for these chariots with hymns of beautiful praise.
For then, through the fortresses of Dakṣa, you two possess wondrous poetic insights;
by the signal of men, O you of purified skill, you take notice.
O Earth, that is the great cosmic order (*ṛta*) of the seers who seek renown; they flow widely over the two vast expanses on their journeys.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you whose eyes reach far, may we and our wise patrons come before you;
may we strive for your sovereign dominion, which is most expansive and provides manifold protection.
Truly, O Ādityas, you have attained here, O gods, the established, lofty, and holy domain;
O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, you have attained the most exalted sovereignty.
When you two, Varuṇa and Mitra, sit upon your golden seat,
you who are the sustainers of the peoples, O destroyers of enemies, grant us your favor.
For all the All-knowing ones—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—follow their sacred laws like footsteps; they protect the mortal from harm.
For they are true, touching the cosmic order (*ṛta*), upholders of *ṛta* among every people; they are excellent leaders, bountiful givers, who create wide space even from distress.
Who indeed among your own persons has praised you, O Mitra and Varuṇa?
This prayer of ours seeks you; this prayer from the Atris seeks you.
Sing forth with an inspired song to Mitra and Varuṇa; they possess great sovereignty and uphold the lofty cosmic order.
The two sovereign kings who have ghee as their source, both Mitra and Varuṇa,
are the gods praised among the gods.
Be able to grant us that great wealth, both earthly and celestial;
for great is your dominion among the gods.
They honor the cosmic order with the cosmic order; they have attained impetuous skill.
The two guileless gods prosper.
O Lords of the rain-giving heaven and the flowing waters, masters of the bountiful earth,
you have taken your seat upon the lofty throne.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, you two uphold the three luminous realms, the three heavens, and the three regions; increasing in power, you protect the dominion of the sovereign and his unaging law.
O Varuṇa, your two milch-cows yield nourishing food; O Mitra, your rivers pour forth honeyed sweetness.
Three radiant bulls, the bestowers of seed, stand over the three worlds.

At dawn I call aloud to the goddess Aditi; at midday and at the rising of the sun, O Mitra and Varuṇa, for wealth and for complete well-being, for our children and progeny, grant us peace and prosperity.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two who are the upholders of the radiant realm, of heaven, and of the earth— neither the immortal gods nor others violate your firm and eternal laws.
For even from afar, O Varuṇa, your aid is indeed present;
O Mitra, may I now win your favor.
O you two who are free from malice, may we rightly obtain that nourishment from you for our sustenance;
O Rudras, may we be yours.
O Rudras, protect us with your protections and save us, O excellent deliverers; may we overcome the Dasyus with our own bodies.
O you of wondrous power, may we not suffer for a spell through our own bodies;
may we not suffer through our offspring nor through our progeny.
Come to us with your great power, O Varuṇa and Mitra, destroyers of enemies;
come to this beautiful sacrifice.
For you two, Varuṇa and Mitra, being far-sighted, rule over the universe;
as lords, cause our prayers to swell with fulfillment.
Come to our pressed juice, O Varuṇa and Mitra, to the donor,
for the drinking of this Soma.
Like Atri, we offer with songs of praise to Mitra and Varuṇa;
sit down upon the sacred grass for the drinking of the Soma.
By your sacred vow you are firm in peace; by your law you bring people into harmony.
Sit down upon the sacrificial grass for the drinking of Soma.
May Mitra and Varuṇa both graciously accept our sacrifice for the sake of our desire;
may they sit down upon the sacred grass to drink the Soma.
Whether you are today in the far distance, O Aśvins, or whether you are nearby; or whether you are in many places, O you who enjoy many things, or in the intermediate space—come hither!
Hither come those two who are most manifold in being, bearing many wondrous deeds;
I call upon the two irresistible ones, the most powerful, for the sake of the desirable prize and for our enjoyment.
In one place you have fixed a beautiful wheel upon your chariot for its beauty;
with the other [wheel], you fly through the realms by your greatness, bypassing the generations of Nahuṣa.
Truly, this deed of yours is well-performed, since all songs of praise follow after you both;
though born separately and stainless, you have entered into kinship with us.
When Sūryā mounted your chariot that always speeds swiftly,
the ruddy birds protected you from the burning heat of the sun.
Atri is mindful of you both, O Heroes, with a heart full of goodwill,
when he busies himself with the stainless *gharma* offering for you by means of his mouth, O Nāsatyas.
Fierce, preeminent, and swift, your continuous roar is heard during your journeys,
O Aśvins, when Atri brings you here with his wondrous deeds, O heroes.
O Rudras, lovers of sweetness, may the swelling draught of honey attend you,
when you carry across the ocean and bring to you ripe nourishments.
Truly, O Aśvins, they call you both the bringers of joy;
you who are most worthy of being invoked at the start of the journey, and most gracious upon the journey.
May these most peaceful prayers, which we have fashioned like chariots, be a source of increase for the Aśvins; we have uttered this great homage.
O divine Aśvins, you who possess the wealth of thought from heaven, Kūṣṭha calls upon you today; O lords of rain-wealth, hear that call, for Atri seeks to win you over.
Where are those two? Where indeed are the famous Nāsatyas, the gods in heaven?
With which people do you take your course, or who is it that is with you among the rivers?
To whom do you go? To whom indeed do you approach? Toward whom do you yoke your chariot?
In whose sacred hymns do you take delight? We desire you both for our protection.
For you two, O Paura, quicken even the city submerged in water for the sake of the city-dweller,
when he is seized in the lair of the malicious one like a lion.
From Cyavāna, who was worn out by age, you stripped away his skin as if it were a garment;
when you made him young again, he regained the desire of a bride.
For here is your praiser; we are present for your glorious sight. Now hear me and come to us with your aids, O you who possess abundant wealth.
Who among the many mortals has won you today? Who, O you who are borne by inspired hymns, is the sage? Who, O lords of wealth, with sacrifices?
O Aśvins, may your chariot—the swiftest among chariots—come hither; though it passes far away, let our hymn of praise reach you, seeking you among mortals.
May our praise be well-received by you two who long for the honeyed draught;
O wise ones, fly hitherward with your winged steeds like two falcons.
O Aśvins, whenever you might hear this invocation, may your excellent enjoyments be ours; indeed, your gifts are abundant.
O Aśvins, lovers of sweetness, the Ṛṣi who praises you adorns himself with a hymn of praise for your most beloved chariot—the vigorous, wealth-bearing vehicle. Hear my invocation!
Come forth, O Aśvins, beyond all the tribes;
O wonder-workers on golden paths, most gracious ones borne by the rivers, lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O Aśvins, bringing us treasures, come to us—
you two Rudras who travel on golden paths, you who possess wealth in horses, lovers of sweetness— take pleasure in my call and hear me!
O you of excellent praise, possessors of bull-like wealth, the voice is placed upon your chariot like a quill.
And your towering, wondrous beast provides nourishment; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
With awakened minds, eager for the chariot, and hearing our invocation, O Aśvins, you come down with your birds to Cyavāna, who is free from duplicity; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O Heroes, may your mind-yoked horses, with their spotted backs, carry you here like birds for the drinking, together with your favors, O Aśvins; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O Aśvins, come hither; O Nāsatyas, do not disregard me. Even past the path of the noble one, go on your circuit, O undeceivable ones; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
At this sacrifice, O undeceivable Lords of Splendor, you two Aśvins attend upon the singer who seeks your aid; O lovers of sweetness, hear my invocation.
Dawn has appeared with her radiant cattle; Agni, the seasonal one, has been established.
O wonder-workers, masters of wealth, your immortal chariot has been yoked. O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
Agni shines forth as the face of the dawns; the god-seeking voices of the sages have risen up.
O Aśvins, come now hither on your chariot toward this overflowing draught of warm milk.
The two who travel most swiftly do not measure out their prepared course; truly, O Aśvins, you come here to this place of praise.
At the arrival of day, you are the swiftest to come with help; you are the most beneficent in turning back misfortune for the donor.
And come at the time of gathering, in the morning, at midday, and at the rising of the sun;
by day and by night with your most peaceful aid—O Aśvins, let not the drinking now be delayed.
For this, O Aśvins, has been your dwelling and home from of old; these are the houses, this is the inner chamber.
Come to us from the lofty heaven, from the mountain, and from the waters, bringing nourishment and strength.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid of the Aśvins, under their excellent guidance.
O Immortals, bring to us wealth, heroic sons, and all auspicious fortunes.
Worship first those who travel at dawn; let them drink before the greedy and stingy.
For the Aśvins accept the sacrifice at dawn; the sages praise them as the first recipients of the offering.
Worship the Aśvins at dawn; urge them forward, for the evening sacrifice is not pleasing to the gods.
Moreover, another besides us sacrifices; each earlier sacrificer prevails more than the one who comes later.
With golden skin, honey-colored, dripping with ghee, your chariot comes rolling toward us, carrying nourishment;
O Aśvins, it is as swift as thought and fleet as the wind, by which you pass over all difficulties.
He who has served most abundantly for the two Nāsatyas and who gives the sweetest portion of food at the distribution—
he shall protect his offspring with blessings and shall ever overcome those whose radiance does not rise upward.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid and excellent guidance of the Aśvins.
O Immortals, bring to us wealth, heroic sons, and all auspicious fortunes.
O Aśvins, come here; O Nāsatyas, do not be averse to us.
Fly hither like two swans to the pressed juices.
O Aśvins, like two deer, like two wild oxen following the pasture,
fly hither like two swans to the pressed juices.
O Aśvins, possessors of abundant wealth, may you enjoy this sacrifice for our success;
like two swans, fly hither to the pressed soma.
When Atri, descending into the *ṛbīsa*, called upon you both like a woman in distress,
O Aśvins, you came with the swiftest and most recent speed of even a hawk.
Open wide, O Lord of the Forest, like the womb of a woman about to give birth.
Hear my call, O Aśvins, and release Saptavadhri!
For the terrified and imploring seer Saptavadhri,
O Aśvins, you two by means of your wondrous powers both joined together and then split apart the tree.
Just as the wind stirs a lotus pond on every side,
so may your embryo stir and come forth, ten months old.
Just as the wind, just as the forest, just as the ocean trembles,
so do you, O ten-month-old one, come forth together with the afterbirth.
Having lain for ten months within his mother,
may the boy come forth alive and uninjured— alive from the living woman.
O Dawn, radiant as the sun, awaken us today for great wealth,
just as you have awakened us before for Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born one, rich in horses and noble gifts.
O Daughter of Heaven, who didst shine forth for Sunītha Śaucadratha,
do thou shine forth for Sahīyas Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born one, rich in horses and noble gifts!
May she, the bringer of wealth, dawn upon us today, O Daughter of Heaven—
she who shone forth for Sahīyas, for Satyaśravas, for Vāyya, O well-born one, rich in horses and in bounty!

O resplendent one, those priests who praise you with hymns— O bountiful lady, O well-born one, mistress of horses and true gifts— may they be rich in splendor, possessing liberal rewards, and be masters of excellent gifts.
For even if these throngs of yours do not please you for the granting of wealth,
they have nevertheless offered their desires around you, O noble-born one, bountiful with horses, as you bestow unashamed riches.
Bestow upon these patrons, O wealthy Dawn, glory accompanied by heroes—
upon those liberal lords who have bestowed upon us unashamed gifts, O well-born one, rich in horses and true speech!
O liberal Dawn, bring great splendor and high renown to them, those wise patrons who, O noble-born one, rich in horses and true to your gifts, share with us wealth in steeds and cattle.
And bring us food accompanied by cattle, O Daughter of Heaven,
together with the rays of the sun, with bright and glowing beams— O well-born one, rich in horses and gifts!
Shine forth, O daughter of heaven; do not delay in spreading thy waters.
Let not the sun scorch thee with his flame as if thou wert a thief or an enemy, O well-born one, rich in horses!
O Uṣas, you ought to grant us this much, or even more— you who, O radiant one,
never fail those who praise you as you shine forth, O well-born one, rich in horses and boons.

The sages praise with their hymns the goddess Uṣas, who illumines the sky, who is vast and true to the cosmic order (ṛta), who possesses ruddy waters, who shines forth, and who brings the light of heaven.
This one, beautiful to behold, awakening the people, making the paths easy to travel, goes at the head;
lofty and great, stirring all things, Dawn bestows light at the beginning of days.
Yoking herself with ruddy kine, this goddess, never failing, has brought us wealth that does not perish.
Cleaving paths for our well-being, she shines forth, much-praised, possessing all boons.
This one becomes a dappled deer, doubly great, revealing her body in the east;
she follows the path of *ṛta* perfectly, as if knowing it well, and does not miss the directions.
Like a bright woman conscious of her body, she has stood up for us to behold, as if bathing in the heights;
driving away hatred and the darknesses, Uṣas, the daughter of heaven, has come with her light.
This daughter of heaven, facing toward men like a blessed maiden, unbinds her garment;
revealing precious things for the donor, the youthful one has brought back the light as of old.

The inspired priests harness their mind and harness their thoughts for the sake of the great, inspired, and wise one. He alone, the knower of the sacred ordinances, ordains the priestly functions; vast indeed is the praise of the god Savitṛ.
The Seer puts on all forms; he has sent forth what is auspicious for bipeds and quadrupeds.
Savitar, the one to be chosen, has looked out upon the firmament; he shines following the departure of the Dawn.
After whose departure other gods have followed according to the greatness of the god by his might— he,
the divine Savitṛ, the steed Etaśa, has measured out the earthly realms by his majesty.
And you go, O Savitṛ, to the three luminous realms; you are united with the rays of the sun. And you encompass the night on both sides; and by your divine laws, O God, you become Mitra.
And you alone are the lord of procreation; furthermore, O God, you become Pūṣan through your journeys.
And you rule over this entire world; Śyāvāśva has brought this hymn of praise to you, O Savitṛ.
We choose that nourishment of the divine Savitṛ;
we meditate upon the most excellent, all-sustaining, and swift bounty of Bhaga.
For no one diminishes this most glorious and beloved sovereign rule of Savitṛ.
For Savitṛ, as Bhaga, bestows treasures upon the donor;
him we implore for that wondrous portion.
O God Savitṛ, impel for us today auspicious fortune accompanied by progeny;
drive away evil dreams.
O God Savitṛ, drive all misfortunes far away;
send us that which is auspicious.
Sinless, under the impulse of the divine Savitṛ and for the sake of Aditi,
may we obtain all desirable things from you both.
Today we choose with hymns the Lord of the True, who belongs to all the gods, Savitṛ, whose impulse is truth.
He who goes before these two days, never failing,
the self-dependent god Savitṛ.
Savitar is he who makes all these created beings hear his proclamation by means of his song, and he impels them forward.
Speak toward the mighty one with these songs; praise Parjanya and win him over with homage.
Bellowing like a bull that gives life-giving rain, he deposits his seed as a germ within the plants.
He strikes down the trees and he strikes down the demons; the entire world trembles before him with his great weapon.
Even the innocent man flees from the one possessing such virile power, when Parjanya, thundering, strikes down the evildoers.
Like a charioteer lashing his horses with a whip, he makes his rain-bearing messengers manifest;
from afar the roar of the lion rises up when Parjanya makes the sky rainy.
The winds blow forth, the lightnings fly; the plants shoot up and the sky overflows.
Refreshing nourishment is born for the whole world when Parjanya protects the earth with his seed.
He under whose ordinance the earth bows down, under whose ordinance the hoofed cattle quiver,
and under whose ordinance the plants are of every form— O Parjanya, grant us great protection.
O Maruts, grant us rain from heaven; cause the streams of the stallion to swell.
Come hither with this thundering, pouring down the waters, you who are our father and the Asura.
Roar out, thunder, and deposit the embryo; fly around with your water-laden chariot.
Draw forth the loosened leather bag downward; let the heights and the depths become level.
Draw up the great reservoir and pour it down; let the released channels flow forward.
Drench heaven and earth with clarified butter; let there be a good drinking-place for the cows.
O Parjanya, when you roar and thunder, striking down the evildoers,
all this world rejoices at it— whatever exists upon the earth.
You have rained down rain; lift it up and seize it! You have made the deserts passable.
You have generated the plants for the sake of nourishment, and you have found wisdom for all creatures.
Truly, O Pṛthivī, you bear the heavy burden of the mountains;
you who, possessing great power, quicken the earth with your might, O most mighty one.
O far-reaching one, hymns of praise resound toward you through the nights—
you who, O bright one, send forth the swelling flood like a neighing steed.
You who, by your might, firmly sustain even the great trees upon the earth;
when from the cloud and the lightning of heaven your rains pour down.
Sing forth a lofty, profound, and beloved prayer to Varuṇa, the renowned sovereign;
he who has spread out the earth for the sun to rest upon, as a butcher spreads out a hide.
In the forests he has spread out the mid-air; he placed speed in the horses, milk in the cows;
Varuṇa placed will in hearts, fire in the waters, the sun in heaven, and Soma on the mountain.
Varuṇa has released the water-skin with its opening turned downward toward the two worlds and the mid-air;
with it, the king of the entire universe moistens the earth as rain does the barley.
He moistens the earth, the broad ground, and the sky as soon as Varuṇa desires the milked [rain] to come.
Then the mountains clothe themselves in clouds, and the powerful heroes exert their strength.
I shall proclaim this great cosmic power (*māyā*) of the renowned Varuṇa, the son of the Asuras: he who, as if by measure, stands in the mid-air and has measured out the earth with the sun.
No one indeed has ever dared to withstand this great creative power of the most wise god:
that the bright rivers, flowing like a single flood, fill the ocean with their waters while pouring them in.

O Varuṇa, whatever offense we have committed against one who is worthy of honor, or against a friend, or even a brother, or against a neighbor— whether a constant companion or a stranger— loosen that from us.
Whatever the gamblers have cheated at play, or whatever we have done in truth, or whatever we do not know—all that, O God Varuṇa, loosen like something slack; then may we be dear to you.
O Indra and Agni, that mortal whom you both protect in battles,
he shall shatter even the firmest strongholds as Trita broke through the enclosures for the sake of the cattle.
Those who are invincible in battles, those who are worthy of renown in the contests for booty,
those who are superior to the five tribes— Indra and Agni, those we invoke.
The terrible power of those two lords is indeed like lightning; from the hands of the bounteous ones, the Vṛtra-slayer hurls his sharp bolt upon the wooden shaft for the sake of the cattle.
In this pursuit of chariots, we invoke you both, O Indra and Agni—
the lords of swift bounty, the wise ones, most fond of hymns.
Increasing day by day for the mortal, those two undeceivable gods—
though they are worthy of worship— I place before me like two portions for a steed.
Thus has this strengthening oblation been offered to Indra and Agni by the pressing-stones, purified like clarified butter.
O you two, bestow great renown upon our patrons, and bestow wealth and nourishment upon those who sing your praises.
May your thoughts go forth to the great Viṣṇu, who is accompanied by the Maruts, born of the mountains, whose movement is swift;
may they go forth to the host that is worthy of sacrifice, joy-giving, powerful, praised for its offerings, and whose law is to shake, unto that strength.
Those who have been born in greatness, and those who now proclaim it themselves through their own wisdom—O Evayāmarut!
That power of yours, O Maruts, cannot be assailed by will; in its giving and its majesty, they are unassailable like the mountains.
They who are heard from afar with song from the lofty heaven, the brilliant and powerful ones, O Evayāmarut;
they whose station no enemy can master, like fires with their own lightning, they rush forward, the roarers of the thundering hosts.
That wide-striding one has stepped forth from the great common seat, O Evayāmarut, when he has yoked himself by his own power upon his lofty heights;
he who vies with others and is of vast splendor comes, increasing our welfare, together with his heroic men.
Like your roar, the mighty bull, the impetuous and powerful one, has caused all to tremble—O Evayāmarut!
With him, they advance, victorious and self-luminous; their reins are firm, their chariots golden, well-armed and swift.
Boundless is your greatness, O you of increased might; let your brilliant power protect us, O Evayāmarut!
For you stand as defenders when we are in peril; as you are visible, deliver us from reproach, shining like fires.
May those Rudras, who are like well-kindled fires and possess abundant splendor, protect us—O Evayāmarut!
The earthly dwelling has spread out long and wide for them, whose hosts are great in their marches, they who are free from sin.
O Maruts, free from hatred, find a path for us; hear the call of the singer, O Evayāmarut!
Like charioteers, you who are of one mind with the great Viṣṇu, ward off our enemies far away by your wondrous powers.
O you who are worthy of sacrifice, come to our well-prepared oblation; hear our call, O you who are unassailable and whose march is swift with the Maruts!
Like the highest mountains in the sky, O wise ones, may you be those whom the reviler cannot hold back.
